news.Title: 群聯法說會》 最高砸近46億元買庫藏股  執行長：對公司未來有信心
news.Content:
NAND控制晶片大廠群聯（8299）今日召開第三季法人說明會，第三季稅後賺破305億元，一年翻12倍，針對董事會拍板要買回2000張庫藏股，執行長潘健成表示，近期股市雜音多，用行動展現對未來的信心。

台股今（6）日盤中一度崩跌近4,000 點，記憶體控制晶片廠群聯（8299）儘管前三季繳出大賺超過32個股本的亮眼成績單，仍難逃市場賣壓波及；盤中最深一度跌至1,405元的跌停價，隨後跌幅收斂，終場下跌 60 元、以 1,500元作收，跌幅 3.85％。

為提振市場信心，群聯董事會今日也拍板最新庫藏股計畫。預計自今年11月6日至116年1月5日，買回2,000張，買回區間價格為每股 1,680 元至 2,280 元，也就是最高砸近46億元，群聯表示，若公司股價低於區間價格下限，仍將繼續執行買回，此舉主要目的為轉讓股份予員工。

執行長潘健成指出，會買回庫藏股，主要是鑑於近期股市出現不少雜音，希望透過實際的買回行動，向市場與投資人展現對公司未來營運發展的堅定信心。

受惠AI基礎建設及企業級儲存需求強勁，第三季營收860.76億元，年增374.6%，稅後淨利305.48億元，一年翻12倍，每股稅後盈餘（EPS）高達138元，優於前季118.57元及去年同期10.75元。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: 〈群聯法說〉Q3每股賺138元創高 擬買回2000張庫藏股「展現對營運的信心」
news.Content:
NAND控制晶片大廠群聯(8299-TW)今(6)日召開法說會並公布第三季財報，稅後純益305.48億元，季增16.5%、年增1,272%，每股純益(EPS)達138元，創歷史新高；累計前三季稅後純益719.37億元，年增1,750%，每股純益325.49元，董事會也通過將買回2,000張庫藏股。

群聯執行長潘健成表示，近期股市雖有一些雜音，但希望透過庫藏股計畫，向市場展現對自身營運的信心。第三季全季維持零負債營運，未向銀行借款，帳上仍有200多億元現金，財務體質穩健。

群聯此次庫藏股預計執行期間為11月6日至2027年1月5日，買回價格區間為每股1,680至2,280元，預計買回總金額上限45.6億元，買回股份將轉讓予員工。

群聯第三季合併營收860.76億元，季增26.8%、年增374.6%；毛利率59.7%，季減5.6個百分點、年增27.3個百分點；營業利益328.98億元，季增24.8%、年增2,210%，營業利益率38.2%，季減0.6個百分點、年增30.4個百分點。其中，研發費用達152.88億元，反映持續投入長期技術與產品布局。

潘健成表示，群聯積極投入先進製程研發、光罩費用、AI儲存及邊緣AI平台開發，並延攬關鍵人才、提升員工獎酬，相關投資有助提高高價值產品比重，強化未來競爭力。此外，也將持續擴充研發團隊，未來半年預計招募最多250名工程師，投入AI網路、AI系統、AI PC及客製化控制器等領域，以因應新產品開發及客戶需求。

news.Title: 前3季每股賺破325元仍還逃跌停！千金股群聯宣布買回2千張庫藏股自救
news.Content:
今年前3季狂賺逾「32個股本」卻仍敵不過大盤股災跌停！群聯（8299）今（6）日重訊公告，為維護股東權益並激勵員工向心力，董事會決議將自今（6）日起至明年1月5日止，大手筆實施庫藏股，預計砸下最高45.6億元買回2,000張股票。

根據群聯公布的最新財務數據，今年前三季（1月至9月）營運表現相當亮眼，累計合併營收達1,949.32億元，營業毛利1,208.39億元，營業利益74.11億元，歸屬於母公司業主淨利達719.38億元，累計基本每股盈餘（EPS）高達 325.49元，相當於前三季就賺進超過32個股本。

不過，今日台股盤中一度大跌近4,000點，身為高價千金股的群聯股價也難逃跌停命運，重訊公告，董事會今日迅速拍板買回庫藏股計畫，預計買回期間自今年11月6日至116年1月5日，預計買回2,000張，佔已發行股份總數0.90%，買回區間價格每股1,680元至2,280元，若公司股價低於區間價格下限，將繼續執行買回，買回目的是轉讓股份予員工。

群聯強調，本次買回股份將用於轉讓給員工以提升向心力，若後續股價因市場波動低於預定價格區間下限，公司仍將持續執行買回，藉此在台股劇烈震盪之際展現基本面強勁的穩健底氣。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: Sick of Swings? Same… But History Is on Our Side
news.Content:
The Nasdaq Composite is down more than 4% on Thursday as we write this. Stocks tied to the artificial intelligence (AI) trade, especially chipmakers and data center names, are sliding for a second day, both here and in Asia.

Qualcomm (NASDAQ:QCOM) has fallen sharply after its smartphone chip sales came in below expectations. Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) is lower despite reporting record revenue, and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) is adding to Wednesday's 7% drop.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

The Nasdaq is still below its record close on Oct. 6. And if you own AI-linked stocks, including many we've recommended, this week alone may have felt like whiplash. Monday brought another drop. On Tuesday night, stock futures fell as election results came in. Wednesday brought relief. This morning, the red is back.

That's a lot to sit through, whether you started with $1,000 in a few stocks or have built a seven-figure portfolio over decades. Either way, the past month has tested our patience.

TMF co-founder and CEO Tom Gardner has never pretended this part is easy. After his October Quarterly Call, he told members he's "happy to give up fractions of future gains for stability." Even he will trade a little return for some peace of mind.

How Fast the Mood Can Turn

Tuesday night showed how quickly things can change. Stock futures fell at first as results came in, then turned higher overnight.

By Wednesday's close, the Dow had jumped 3%. That was its biggest gain the day after a midterm election since 1982, according to CFRA Research.

Picture selling your stocks at 10 p.m. on Tuesday. By Wednesday's close, you'd likely have missed the rally. Today's drop may tempt some of us to make that same mistake.

Co-founder David Gardner has a line for moments like this: "Stocks always go down faster than they go up, but they always go up more than they go down." The drops feel worse because they come so fast. Historically, though, the gains have been bigger.

Owning many stocks makes those drops easier to live through. The Motley Fool now suggests the average member own at least 50, built up over time. With that many businesses across different industries, it's much harder for any single bad morning to sink you.

AI Isn't One Trade

Not every AI stock joined Wednesday's rally. Cloud giants like Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) jumped. Chipmakers fell, and so did many companies tied to the data center build-out, such as Vertiv (NYSE:VRT), GE Vernova (NYSE:GEV), and Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE). That happened even as most stocks rose.

Story Continues

If you own a cloud giant, Wednesday may have felt great. If you own a chipmaker, you may have watched your stock slide while nearly everything else climbed. That can feel lonely.

But a few rough days for a stock say little about the business behind it. Big tech companies are still spending heavily on AI, and demand for chips still looks strong. Order books at many data center suppliers also appear to be growing fast, though the ride may stay bumpy. If the companies you own keep growing, short-term swings like this one tend to matter less over time.

"AI stocks" covers very different businesses with different risks, so they won't always move together.

That's why it can help to own a mix of AI businesses, not just one kind. When one part of the trade struggles, another may be holding up.

Two Ways to Stay in the Game

If today's drop has you itching to act, two habits can help. They apply just as well whether you're investing $300 or $30,000.

First, aim to hold for at least three to five years as a minimum. One rough week, or even one disappointing quarter, tells you little about where a business will be by then. When you think in years, an overnight futures move gets much easier to ignore.

Second, keep new bets small. Try a small position in an idea that interests you. If it works out, great. If it doesn't, you've learned something without putting much of your long-term plan at risk.

The Long View

The past month has been uncomfortable, and the swings may not be over yet. We won't pretend otherwise.

But it helps to zoom out. Over the long run, the stock market has historically climbed up and to the right. Since 1874, U.S. stocks have returned about 11% in an average year, counting dividends, according to our research . Past performance does not guarantee future results. Still, that history includes wars, recessions, crashes, and plenty of months like this one.

The Motley Fool's goal is to help you beat the market over time, with a portfolio you don't lose sleep over and actually enjoy owning. That's the goal for us individually, too.

news.Title: Big Tech's massive AI spending is causing another problem for investors
news.Content:
The bottom-line-padding, stock-price-fueling stock buyback from hyperscalers may now be on pause as they spend aggressively on AI infrastructure.

Combined buybacks for Alphabet ( GOOGL ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Meta ( META ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Oracle ( ORCL ) — aka the country's main AI hyperscalers — fell to a mere $4.4 billion in the third quarter, per numbers crunched by the Kobeissi Letter. This marks the lowest dollar amount spent dating back to the third quarter of 2017. The third quarter also represented the third straight quarter buybacks have been below $5 billion.

Share repurchases for this group have dropped a stunning 90% since the $45.9 billion peak recorded in the fourth quarter of 2021.

"The era of massive Big Tech stock buybacks is over," the Kobeissi Letter team said.

Cash once allocated to buybacks is being funneled into an array of AI projects at the hyperscalers.

The numbers on AI capex are getting more staggering by the day.

Combined capital expenditures for Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, and Oracle are tracking toward approximately $800 billion in 2026.

This unprecedented infrastructure sprint is fueled by aggressive investments in power generation, data centers, and advanced AI accelerators.

Wall Street analysts project the cohort's aggregate capital spending will surge past $1.2 trillion in 2027.

news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Microsoft ( NASDAQ:MSFT ) has decided not to expand a major AI computing agreement with UK startup Nscale, walking away from an option that could have been worth tens of billions of dollars .

The decision affects additional capacity at a Texas data center where Microsoft already has a contract with Nscale. Importantly, the existing agreement remains in place. Microsoft's decision not to exercise the expansion option was made several months ago, before Nscale filed for an IPO in September.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Sign with MSFT.

Is MSFT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The companies had previously agreed for Nscale to deploy around 200,000 Nvidia AI chips across data centers in the U.S. and Europe.

Nscale disclosed in its IPO filing that statements of work signed with Microsoft between September 2025 and April 2026 were worth up to about $43.8 billion through 2033 , excluding optional extensions.

The rejected Texas expansion would reportedly have covered about 500 megawatts of additional capacity , potentially adding billions of dollars of future revenue for Nscale. The startup now needs to find other customers for that capacity.

That adds to a growing list of execution challenges.

Microsoft previously pulled out of plans to anchor Nscale's flagship data-center project in Essex after power-connection delays pushed expected supply into the 2030s. Nscale is also developing a massive West Virginia campus tied to a potential $45 billion Anthropic deal , but that project faces substantial financing and construction requirements.

Still, Nscale says the Microsoft decision does not affect the roughly $103 billion of total contract value disclosed in its IPO filing. The company is already in talks with other major customers for the unused Texas capacity.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most important point is that this does not necessarily mean Microsoft is pulling back from AI spending broadly .

The company is declining an optional expansion with one infrastructure provider. Its existing Nscale Texas contract remains intact.

That makes this look more like a project-specific discipline story than clear evidence of weakening AI demand.

For Nscale, however, the timing is difficult.

The company is trying to support a planned IPO reportedly valued around $35 billion , while investors are already questioning the financing needs and execution risk surrounding AI infrastructure businesses.

For investors, the key things to watch are whether Nscale quickly replaces Microsoft with another customer, whether Anthropic expands its relationship, financing progress in West Virginia, and whether Microsoft makes similar cuts with other AI infrastructure partners .

One rejected option does not break the AI spending boom.

But for Nscale, it raises the pressure considerably.

news.Title: MKSI Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates on Strong Semiconductor Growth
news.Content:
MKS Inc. MKSI reported third-quarter 2026 non-GAAP earnings of $4.18 per share, up 116.6% year over year. The figure beat the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 14.84%.

Revenues surged 43% year over year to $1.41 billion and surpassed the consensus mark by 4.12%. Growth was driven by robust demand across Semiconductor and Electronics & Packaging, supported by AI-related investments. Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 30.7%, reflecting improved operating leverage and stronger profitability.

MKSI's Q3 Revenue Mix Strengthens

Product revenues, which accounted for 89.5% of total revenues, increased 47% year over year to $1.26 billion. The performance reflected strong demand across the company's semiconductor, electronics and packaging, and specialty industrial end markets.

Services revenues totaled $149 million, representing 10.5% of revenues. The figure increased 16.4% from the year-ago quarter, contributing to the company's broad-based top-line growth.

MKS Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

MKS Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | MKS Inc. Quote

MKS' End Markets Deliver Robust Growth

Semiconductor revenues surged 53.7% year over year to $638 million and represented 45.2% of total revenues. Management highlighted accelerating AI-driven demand across semiconductor manufacturing and advanced packaging applications, supported by robust orders and new design wins.

Electronics & Packaging revenues increased 43.6% to $415 million, contributing 29.4% of revenues. Specialty Industrial revenues rose 26.8% to $360 million and accounted for 25.5% of the quarterly total. Management noted that revenues across all three end markets were at or above the high end of guidance, underscoring broad demand strength.

MKSI's Operating Details

For the third quarter of 2026, gross margin expanded 110 basis points year over year to 47.7%.

Non-GAAP operating expenses were $281 million compared with $256 million a year earlier. The increase in expenses accompanied substantial revenue growth, allowing the company to generate stronger operating leverage.

Adjusted EBITDA climbed 80.8% year over year to a record $434 million. Adjusted EBITDA margin rose 640 basis points to 30.7%, reflecting higher revenues and improved profitability.

Non-GAAP operating income increased 91.7% to $393 million, while the non-GAAP operating margin improved 700 basis points to 27.8%. GAAP income from operations increased to $326 million from $138 million in the prior-year quarter. The operating margin expanded 910 basis points to 23.1%, benefiting from the higher revenue base and gross margin improvement.

Story Continues

MKSI's Cash Flow and Balance Sheet Improve

As of Sept. 30, 2026, MKS had cash and cash equivalents of $676 million compared with $611 million as of June 30, 2026.

As of Sept. 30, 2026, long-term debt totaled $2.38 billion.

Net cash provided by operating activities was $292 million in the third quarter, up 48.2% year over year.

MKS' Q4 Outlook Points to Continued Momentum

For the fourth quarter of 2026, MKS expects revenues of $1.49 billion, plus or minus $40 million. Gross margin is projected to be 47.5%, plus or minus 1 percentage point, while non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be $288 million, plus or minus $5 million.

The company forecasts non-GAAP earnings of $5 per share, plus or minus 38 cents. Non-GAAP net earnings are projected to be $352 million, plus or minus $27 million.

Adjusted EBITDA is expected to reach $461 million, plus or minus $29 million.

MKSI's Zacks Rank & Other Stocks to Consider

MKSI currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).

Some other top-ranked stocks in the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector include Cisco Systems CSCO, Analog Devices ADI and NVIDIA NVDA. Each stock presently carries a Zacks Rank #2. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Shares of Analog Devices have risen 49.7% year to date. Analog Devices is set to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on Nov. 24.

news.Title: Snowflake Soars 32% Year to Date: Buy, Sell, or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Snowflake SNOW shares have gained 32.5% year to date, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's 9% gain and the Zacks Internet Software industry's 3.5% decline.

The company's shares have also outperformed its peers, including major players like Oracle ORCL, Broadcom AVGO and Amazon AMZN, which are also expanding their footprint in the AI space. While Oracle and AVGO shares have plunged 36.5% and 6%, respectively, Amazon shares have gained 15.2% year to date.

The outperformance can be attributed to SNOW's strong AI adoption and increasing usage of its platform, as reflected by the net revenue retention rate of 126% in the second quarter of fiscal 2027. These factors are helping SNOW fend off competitors like Oracle, Broadcom and Amazon.

SNOW Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

SNOW Benefits From Expanding AI Portfolio

Snowflake is benefiting from an expanding AI portfolio. The company has rapidly broadened its suite of AI-powered products, including CoCo and CoWork, which are seeing strong adoption across a diverse customer base. The company launched more than 330 generally available product capabilities during the first half, including Cortex Sense and Cortex AI Gateway, strengthening its ability to offer governed AI, model choice and agentic workflows.

Building on this momentum, the company recently introduced major enhancements to its CoCo coding agent and CoWork personal AI agent, enabling enterprises to automate complex workflows using governed business data. The new always-on CoCo and CoWork Bots autonomously execute tasks, requiring human intervention only for critical decisions or approvals.

The innovations support integrations with Slack, Excel, Google Sheets and mobile devices, while introducing automation, memory and shared AI workflows. Snowflake also unveiled Cortex Training for customizing AI models and optimizing costs. CoWork is used by more than 5,800 accounts, while CoCo serves more than 9,100 accounts.

Further expanding its enterprise AI portfolio, Snowflake introduced new AI capabilities designed to help enterprises deploy autonomous agents with trusted business context, enhanced security, and centralized governance. The new Business Ontology feature within Snowflake Horizon Catalog enables AI agents to access consistent, pre-approved business definitions, improving accuracy and reliability. The company also expanded Cortex AI Gateway to provide unified controls for agent activities, model access, security, compliance and spending. Additional capabilities include Cortex Sandboxes, Agent Abuse Detection and Dynamic Model Routing. Enterprises including Glean and Kargo are leveraging Cortex AI Gateway, while dentsu and Merkle are adopting Business Ontology to strengthen AI-driven operations.

Strong AI demand is improving Snowflake's financial outlook. For fiscal 2027, the company raised product revenue guidance to $6.07 billion, implying 36% year-over-year growth compared with the previous outlook of $5.84 billion and 31% growth. Fiscal third-quarter product revenues are expected to be between $1.588 billion and $1.593 billion, indicating 37-38% growth.

Story Continues

SNOW Benefits From Expanding Customer Base

Snowflake is benefiting from an expanding customer base, strong adoption among large enterprises and rising consumption across its AI Data Cloud. In the second quarter of fiscal 2027, SNOW had 14,554 total customers, up 32% year over year, after adding 692 net new customers. The company also added 14 Forbes Global 2000 customers, taking the total to 829, or more than 41% of the Global 2000.

Snowflake is also witnessing deeper engagement from existing customers. Large-customer momentum remained strong, with 828 customers generating more than $1 million in trailing 12-month product revenues, up 27% year over year. Another 65 customers exceeded $10 million in trailing product revenues.

Sustained customer additions, deeper enterprise penetration and increasing AI adoption are expected to support Snowflake's growth prospects. In the second quarter of 2026, remaining performance obligations increased 30% year over year to $9 billion, with roughly 54% expected to be recognized as revenue over the next 12 months.

SNOW Offers Positive Guidance

Snowflake's rich customer base and innovative AI portfolio are expected to drive the company's top-line growth.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fiscal third-quarter revenues is currently pegged at $1.65 billion, indicating 36.08% year-over-year growth.

The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at 60 cents per share, which has been unchanged over the past 30 days. This suggests an increase of 71.43% year over year.

SNOW Trades at a Premium

Snowflake shares are currently overvalued, as suggested by its Value Score of F.

SNOW stock is trading at a premium with a forward 12-month Price/Sales of 13.44X compared with the Internet Software industry's 3.8X.

SNOW Valuation

Conclusion

Snowflake's accelerating AI adoption, strong enterprise momentum and raised product revenue guidance support a positive outlook for the stock. These factors have justified its premium valuation.

news.Title: GNRC's Amazon Deal Adds $2.4 Billion in Data Center Revenue Visibility
news.Content:
Generac Holdings Inc . GNRC has added a major multiyear demand anchor through its long-term Amazon supply agreement. Initial deliveries are expected to total a combined $2.4 billion in 2027 and 2028.

Generac Holdings Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Generac Holdings Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Generac Holdings Inc. Quote

The agreement strengthens visibility into Generac's fast-growing data center business, but it also raises the operational stakes. Capacity, engine sourcing and margins will matter as the company attempts to scale output rapidly.

GNRC's Amazon Deal Deepens Data Center Exposure

The Amazon agreement covers backup power generators for data centers and materially expands Generac's forward demand base. It arrives as data centers become one of the company's most important Commercial & Industrial growth markets.

The broader market is attracting other power suppliers as well. Cummins Inc . CMI is expanding its data center power presence through generator and battery-storage projects, illustrating the intensity of spending around mission-critical power infrastructure.

Generac's Backlog Signals Multiyear Revenue Visibility

Generac's data center backlog reached roughly $4.5 billion in the third quarter, nearly tripling from $1.6 billion in July 2026. The company also secured nearly $600 million of non-hyperscale orders during the quarter.

Generac Holdings Inc. Revenue (Quarterly)

Generac Holdings Inc. revenue-quarterly | Generac Holdings Inc. Quote

That diversification matters because it broadens demand beyond a single hyperscale customer. Management expects nearly $500 million of data center revenues in 2026 and more than $2 billion in 2027, giving the backlog a clear near-term conversion path.

GNRC's Capacity Expansion Becomes More Critical

Initial production at Generac's Sussex, WI, large-megawatt generator facility began near the end of the third quarter. The company plans a substantial production ramp and expects its Belvidere, IL, packaging facility to come online in early 2027.

The Enercon acquisition is intended to deepen vertical integration, while expansions in Europe, Asia and Latin America support international demand. Eaton Corporation plc ETN is also expanding data center-related manufacturing, reflecting how infrastructure suppliers are adding capacity to serve the same broad buildout.

Generac's Deal Economics Come With New Risks

Management expects consolidated gross margin to decline sequentially to 37-38% in the fourth quarter as data center sales become a larger part of the mix.

Story Continues

Generac Holdings Inc. Gross Margin (TTM)

Generac Holdings Inc. gross-margin-ttm | Generac Holdings Inc. Quote

Amazon also received warrants for up to 1,693,745 Generac shares at an exercise price of $200.9266. Most of the warrants vest in tranches tied to qualifying payments that can extend to $8 billion over the seven-year term.

GNRC's Near-Term Signals Stay Constructive

The Amazon agreement materially improves revenue visibility, but backlog alone does not remove execution risk. Generac still has to secure engines, ramp plants efficiently and convert orders while protecting profitability.

GNRC currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which points to favorable near-term earnings-estimate dynamics. The stock also has a Momentum Score of A, Growth Score of B and VGM Score of B, adding support to its near-term profile.

The Value Score of C argues for discipline. The data center opportunity is substantial, but the current Style Score mix suggests the stronger case rests on growth and momentum rather than a uniformly cheap valuation.

news.Title: AI Data Center Boom Runs Into a Political Wall
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

The U.S. midterm elections may have created a much tougher regulatory environment for new AI data centers, according to Needham, raising the risk that the next phase of the infrastructure boom becomes slower, more expensive, and more politically complicated.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with META.

Is META fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Needham said the election results produced a hostile regulatory backdrop for new data-center construction, particularly after Democrats gained control of Congress and won several key governorships, including Texas.

That matters because Texas is one of the most important locations in the current AI infrastructure buildout.

Opposition to data centers has increasingly centered on electricity prices, water usage, environmental impact, tax incentives, and whether local communities are being forced to absorb infrastructure costs . Reuters reported that data-center opponents were among the major beneficiaries of the midterm results, including candidates who campaigned on moratoriums or tighter development rules.

The election also showed that the backlash is not limited to one state.

A large number of local ballot measures moved toward restrictions, moratoriums, or tougher operating requirements, signaling that permitting risk is becoming a much broader issue for developers.

But Needham sees an important twist.

Tighter regulation could actually benefit established hyperscalers such as Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ), Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOG ), and Meta ( NASDAQ:META ) .

If new projects become harder to approve, existing permitted capacity becomes more valuable. Slower construction could also reduce future capital-spending estimates without immediately hurting revenue from data centers that are already operating, potentially improving near-term returns on invested capital.

Needham also argues that the biggest hyperscalers are better positioned than newer AI infrastructure companies to navigate political opposition because they have more experience, deeper resources, and stronger government-relations capabilities.

Investor Takeaway

I think the most interesting part of Needham's call is that bad news for data-center construction may not be equally bad for every AI company .

For newer developers, tighter permitting means delays, higher costs, and potentially stranded projects.

For Amazon, Google, and Meta, the same restrictions could make their already-built capacity more valuable while also giving them an excuse to slow capital spending.

Story Continues

That creates a potential shift in the AI trade.

Investors may begin valuing scarce permitted capacity just as highly as future growth plans.

For investors, the key things to watch are state moratoriums, local permitting rules, power-cost policies, hyperscaler capex revisions, and whether projects migrate toward friendlier states or overseas markets .

The AI race still needs more compute.

The political permission to build it may now be the scarcer asset.

news.Title: Microsoft Stock Has Gained More Than 50% in About 4 Months. Here's What It Has Usually Done Next.
news.Content:
Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) shares jumped nearly 7% on Wednesday, Nov. 4, as U.S. stocks rallied the day after Democrats won control of Congress in the midterm elections.

The stock sits near $553 as of this writing. That leaves it about 57% over its June 25 close of $352.83, and the rise took just 92 trading days.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

A move like that is rare for a company worth about $4 trillion. But Microsoft has done it before. Going back through its daily closing prices to 1986, I find 13 past runs like this one. In 11 of them, the stock was up a year later, with a median one-year gain of around 33%.

It's a solid record. But it might mean less than it seems. Microsoft stock has climbed in around 74% of all one-year periods since 1986, fast run or not. And the latest run, in July 2025, is one of the two that finished down.

Image source: Getty Images.

Most of the big years came early

Every run starts the first day Microsoft closed at least 50% over its lowest close in the past 92 trading days. I used split-adjusted prices without dividends, and runs had to begin at least one year apart. "A year later" is the close 12 months after a run started (or the last trading day before it). By this rule, the current run began on Oct. 6.

Ten of the 13 past runs came between 1986 and 2001, when Microsoft was a much smaller company. The biggest years came in that stretch, too. Shares more than doubled over the year after the runs that began in November 1986, January 1991, and March 1998.

The one early miss followed a January 1988 run, when the stock was recovering from the October 1987 crash, and shares were around 12% down a year later.

Since the 2001 run, Microsoft has only moved this fast three times. The stock gained around 12% over the year after June 2009 and about 33% after June 2020. Then it lost about 13% after July 2025.

Even some of the good years were rough. After the January 1992 and January 2001 runs, shares slid over 20% at one point before ending the year higher.

The July 2025 run started at a steep price

Microsoft's latest fast run hit the 50% mark the day after its fiscal 2025 fourth-quarter report on July 30, 2025. The July 31 close of $533.50 was around 50% over the April 8 low. Investors paid about 38 times earnings then, using the $14.13 a share Microsoft earned in fiscal 2025 on a non-GAAP (adjusted) basis.

Story Continues

Shares drifted mostly sideways over a few months. Then they fell all the way to that $352.83 close on June 25, 2026 -- around 34% below where the run began.

Even a 15% gain the day after Microsoft's fiscal 2026 report in late July didn't erase the loss, and on July 31, 2026, shares were still about 13% down from a year earlier.

I'd say the starting price mattered more than the pace of the run. At around 38 times earnings, the shares could fall a long way on any hint of trouble.

Is this run different?

In a couple of ways, I think it is. Adjusted earnings per share grew 22% in fiscal 2026, and the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (which ended Sept. 30, 2026) added another 18% gain, to $4.89. For the past four reported quarters, adjusted earnings were about $18.04 a share. At roughly $553, the stock costs about 31 times adjusted earnings, well under the 38 times earnings investors paid in July 2025.

Azure, Microsoft's cloud computing platform, is also accelerating. Its revenue climbed 40% year over year in the quarter that ended September 2025, then 42% in the quarter that ended this June and 48% in the last one.

Of course, that growth takes a lot of money. Microsoft's cash from operations rose 29% from a year ago. But free cash flow dropped about 27% to $18.6 billion as the company poured more cash into data centers.

What has Microsoft stock usually done after a run like this? It has usually kept rising. But that record only modestly beats the stock's odds in any given year, and the most recent case went the other way.

The business looks stronger than it did in July 2025, and the stock is cheaper relative to its earnings. Still, with free cash flow shrinking, paying about 31 times adjusted earnings just after a 57% run isn't something I'm eager to do.

news.Title: The AI Selloff Is Getting Worse. Nvidia, Dell and Data Center Stocks Are Plunging Hard. Is It Time to Buy the Dip?
news.Content:
Stocks tied to the artificial intelligence buildout fell broadly again in Thursday morning trading. On Wednesday, after Democrats swept the midterm elections, data-center builders and power-equipment makers fell as much as 20% or more, and Dell Technologies (NYSE:DELL), optical-networking makers, and other AI hardware names dropped 7% to 10%, even as the S&P 500 rose. Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) slipped about 3% and Arm Holdings (NASDAQ:ARM) about 5%.

But Thursday was worse for the biggest names. Nvidia's drop nearly doubled to about 6%, and Arm's to about 10%, and this time the broader market fell too, with the S&P 500 down about 1.5% as of roughly 9:55 a.m. ET. The builders and adjacent stocks hit hardest on Wednesday kept falling, though by less, with data-center cooling stock Modine (NYSE:MOD) down 9% after a 21% decline on Wednesday.

Which Stocks Fell?

Many big names felt quite a bit of damage. Nvidia, the chipmaker at the center of the AI boom, fell about 6% to $188.75. Dell, one of the biggest sellers of AI servers, dropped about 9%, erasing about $20 billion in market value, and Arm lost about 10%, another roughly $20 billion. Palantir Technologies (NASDAQ:PLTR), server and component makers Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE), and Celestica (NYSE:CLS) each fell 7% to 8%. Astera Labs (NASDAQ:ALAB), which makes chips that connect AI hardware inside data centers, slid about 11%.

Meanwhile, builders fell for a second day. Comfort Systems USA (NYSE:FIX), a mechanical and electrical contractor with heavy exposure to AI projects, fell about 9%. Argan (NYSE:AGX) lost about 9% and MasTec (NYSE:MTZ) about 8%, both pace for their second drop of 7% or more this month. EMCOR (NYSE:EME) and Dycom (NYSE:DY) were down 6% to 7%.

Also hard hit were optical-networking companies, which make the lasers and equipment that move data across fiber lines, including inside AI data centers. Ciena (NYSE:CIEN) fell about 11%, wiping out about $4.3 billion in value. Applied Optoelectronics (NASDAQ:AAOI) dropped about 13%, and Coherent (NYSE:COHR) and MACOM Technology (NASDAQ:MTSI) fell 9% to 11%.

Several companies that got their start in Bitcoin mining now build or rent out data centers for AI customers, and they fell too. Applied Digital (NASDAQ:APLD), which builds large data centers for AI workloads, fell about 11%. Core Scientific (NASDAQ:CORZ) and Cipher Digital lost roughly 8% to 9%. Meanwhile, Bitcoin itself was down only about 1% through about 10 a.m. ET, signaling that investors weren't selling these stocks over crypto. It wasn't until the broader market started tumbling that Bitcoin also started sliding, down nearly 6% by about 11 a.m. ET.

Story Continues

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Why the Midterms Matter for Data Centers

A big part of the worry is how quickly new data centers can be built, given the blue wave that swept through the Midterm elections. With Democrats now in charge of both chambers, investors are bracing for more oversight of an industry that many governments are already trying to regulate. In Texas, for example, one of the biggest data-center markets, the new governor-elect campaigned on pausing new data-center construction.

UBS analysts put a number on the risk: If construction pauses spread, they estimate that nearly a third of the new U.S. data-center capacity expected to come online in 2028 could be delayed or lost. For companies whose growth is contingent on the supply available to meet booming demand, that's a big deal.

Even Good News Isn't Helping

Perhaps the clearest example of how jumpy investors are is Viavi Solutions (NASDAQ:VIAV), which crashed 18% the morning after it reported that quarterly revenue jumped 57% to $469.3 million, raised its outlook, and approved a $500 million stock buyback.

The firm clearly delivered strong results, but the massive plunge shows the stock is trading on fear about the whole AI build-out rather than the business in particular. That could mean more pain if political news gets worse. But it can also mean the market is throwing out good companies along with the risky ones.

So, Is It Time to Buy the Dip?

For most investors, not all at once. The political risk is real but unsettled. Congress doesn't change hands until January, and any state-level pause would still have to be written and passed. Meanwhile, a 6% drop in Nvidia is a much smaller move than the double-digit losses in fiber makers or Wednesday's plunge in builders, a sign that investors are punishing the companies most exposed to new construction the hardest.

Some see value already. Asset manager VanEck argues the sell-off has left Bitcoin miners oversold because their access to the power grid is scarce and commands a premium for AI customers looking for places to build.

If you believe the AI build-out will keep going, a two-day plunge like this is the kind of moment long-term investors look for. The smarter move is to buy slowly, in pieces, and to favor companies with strong balance sheets and real customer contracts over the most speculative names. Just remember, these are among the most volatile AI stocks in the market right now. And if you'd rather avoid the political risk entirely, there are steadier ways to own tech stocks while Washington sorts this out.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

While everyone watches the chip designers, one "backbone" company provides the critical technology that Nvidia and AMD literally cannot function without. We've detailed this under-the-radar player in our new AI Playbook.

Continue »

news.Title: Microsoft Sours on Neoclouds Amid Data Center Delays, Costs
news.Content:
(Bloomberg) -- Microsoft Corp. helped create the "neocloud" boom, signing tens of billions of dollars in contracts with upstart data center operators in an effort to sate the crushing appetite for its cloud and AI services.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Morgan Stanley Offers $2.3 Billion Debt for Dell Family Deal

Democrats Clinch Huge Wins on Inflation Anger, Trump Fatigue

What the Democrats' Sweep of Congress Means for Trump

Trump Now Has to Govern Through a Midterm Meltdown of His Own Making

DeSantis Calls GOP Midterm Wipeout 'Extinction Level Event'

Now, as neocloud companies grapple with delays, regulatory snags and high costs, some key Microsoft leaders have developed a case of buyer's remorse.

The company is tightening oversight of some data center projects from Nebius Group NV, IREN Ltd., and Nscale Plc, stepping away from ones it deems risky and debating internally whether to ink new neocloud deals, according to people familiar with the matter.

The friction was on display during Microsoft's most-recent earnings call, when Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood said that delays in the delivery of some third-party capacity was disrupting the company's spending plans. It was the third time she has called out such issues on an earnings call.

Some of the recent hiccups involved issues with cabling at a site in Texas being developed by IREN, according to people familiar with the situation. Data center servers are connected by intricate networks of fiber-optic cables. IREN, an Australian firm that pivoted from cryptocurrency to AI in 2023, also suffered a generator fire at the campus in April and disclosed hardware delivery delays there in August.

IREN and Microsoft officials met last week and negotiated a revised timeline that may push back the site's completion by several weeks or months, according to people familiar with the events.

Microsoft manages relationships with infrastructure partners "against our requirements and customer demand, including monitoring delivery and adjusting plans when circumstances change," a company spokesperson said. "These are normal and responsible practices for managing large, complex infrastructure projects, and they help us bring capacity online reliably and efficiently."

IREN declined to comment.

Shares of IREN and Nebius both fell about 20% on Thursday amid a broader selloff of AI infrastructure stocks.

It's a perilous moment for the neoclouds, which were created to capitalize on a shortage of computing power by speeding up the deployment of artificial intelligence infrastructure, including chips from Nvidia Corp.

Story Continues

Industry analyst Gartner Inc. recently estimated that 80% of neocloud providers could be consolidated or closed by the end of the decade. Elon Musk — whose SpaceX also sells computing power — offered a similarly bleak outlook of "guppy-level death" for many neoclouds because they're struggling to raise sufficient funds to operate.

These fears were compounded after a series of victories this week by Democratic candidates for governor, who made more aggressive data center regulation a central part of their campaigns. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa in particular has called for an immediate moratorium on data center development until more thorough regulation is established.

Microsoft was the nascent industry's most crucial early patron, providing the likes of CoreWeave Inc. and Nscale with massive contracts that let them get big quickly. Even though Microsoft has a huge fleet of data centers, it was willing to pay up to meet demand it couldn't handle on its own.

"We've had to pinch our nose and borrow GPUs from some of our competitors," Microsoft Executive Vice President Mat McBride said of the company's neocloud deals during a conference hosted by Evercore in June. "We've done that because we have a very, very strong demand signal."

Each week, CFO Hood chairs a meeting about computing capacity – when it's coming online, from where and which part of the company will get it. A common point of discussion at these sessions is whether the neoclouds' timelines are credible and what Microsoft can do to accelerate them, according to people who've been involved with the meetings.

Increasingly, Microsoft is putting boots on the ground. In recent months, the company has dispatched workers to neocloud sites to make sure facilities are being built to its specifications and following regulations, according to job listings and people familiar with the matter. For example, Microsoft sent workers to a Nebius site in New Jersey that was fined $1 million for running generators without permits. Microsoft has also sent people to projects in Texas being built by Nscale and IREN.

In other cases, Microsoft is walking away from sites it no longer considers tenable, including multiple Nscale projects. It declined to expand its deal with Nscale in Texas, and some of that capacity ended up being taken by Figure AI. Microsoft also stepped away from a letter of intent to lease 1.35 gigawatts from the company in West Virginia.

And last month it cancelled a roughly $3 billion Nscale deal tied to a UK data center owing to multiyear delays in getting grid power, according to people familiar with the deal. Nscale said at the time that the UK withdrawal didn't impact its other deals with Microsoft.

The Information and Financial Times previously reported some details of Microsoft's IREN and Nscale deals.

Microsoft is currently focused on expanding its own data centers rather than adding new neocloud deals, according to those who've spoken with leaders inside the company. The company hasn't entirely sworn off new neocloud deals, but many company leaders express strong reluctance, the people said.

Over the last year, Microsoft has added more than $200 billion of new data center lease commitments. Some of this includes neocloud capacity, according to a spokesperson. All of this spending is being directed toward major expansion of its own server farm capacity in the coming years, Bloomberg previously reported.

Buying third-party computing capacity was always controversial at Microsoft. Executives were concerned that even partial outsourcing would help prop up would-be competitors. They also fretted that Microsoft would be exposed to higher costs and execution risks because neoclouds had limited experience building and operating server farms.

Some of the competition fears came true: CoreWeave hired a handful of key executives from Microsoft, then did a deal directly with close partner OpenAI last year. This rankled many leaders inside Microsoft, according to employees who were present at the time. A CoreWeave spokesperson said that Microsoft was one of its first partners and collaborators, "and we continue to have a great relationship."

Nebius has been unusually upfront with its competitive strategy. It will scale up by inking contracts with big customers like Microsoft or Meta Platforms Inc. knowing that they'll abandon neoclouds in the long run, Nebius CEO Arkady Volozh said during a March conference hosted by Morgan Stanley.

"We treat this business as temporary," Volozh said, referring to his company's deals with customers like Microsoft and Meta. "They just cannot cope with the speed now — that's why they're outsourcing."

Meanwhile, demand for computing power remains much higher than supply — and is expected to for the foreseeable future. So even if Microsoft decides not to sign new neocloud deals, Anthropic PBC and Alphabet Inc.'s Google have been accelerating their own commitments to the upstart data center operators.

--With assistance from Matt Day, Dina Bass and Mark Bergen.

news.Title: Midterm Results Put These 4 Renewable, Healthcare & AI Stocks in Focus
news.Content:
The Nov. 4 U.S. midterm election results have added a new dimension to the U.S. investment landscape. Following the results, the market response has been mixed so far, with renewable energy stocks gaining on expectations of continued policy support. Some AI infrastructure operators and defense contractors faced pressure amid concerns over regulatory scrutiny and spending priorities.

The broader equity market, meanwhile, remained resilient. On Nov. 4, the S&P 500 advanced 1.58%, the Nasdaq Composite gained 1.44% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 3%. However, divergent sector performance suggests that investors are becoming more selective about companies with varying exposure to government policies and regulatory changes.

Beyond the election-related developments, persistent inflation, borrowing costs and uncertainty surrounding corporate capital expenditure continue to shape investment decisions. Potential changes in renewable energy incentives, healthcare funding, AI infrastructure regulations and defense procurement priorities could influence industry growth and earnings prospects.

Against this backdrop, investors may explore opportunities across renewable energy, healthcare, AI infrastructure and semiconductor design, focusing on companies with favorable demand trends, strong earnings prospects and the financial flexibility to keep up with the evolving policy and regulatory conditions.

Policy Uncertainty Creates Opportunities Across Sectors

The immediate market reaction to the midterm results showed mixed responses by industries to changing policy expectations. According to Reuters, sector performance diverged considerably. Solar and clean-energy stocks advanced, whereas defense contractors and several data-center operators came under pressure.

Reuters also stated that gains in Microsoft MSFT, Amazon AMZN and Alphabet GOOGL shares yesterday, alongside declines in Applied Digital, IREN and Core Scientific, reflected investor expectations that tighter scrutiny of AI infrastructure development could slow down data-center expansion. According to the report, this trend could benefit established technology companies while creating financing and growth challenges for smaller data-center operators.

These developments show the importance of distinguishing between companies with strong fundamentals and those whose growth prospects depend heavily on favorable policy conditions.

Renewable Energy, Healthcare & AI Infrastructure in Focus

Renewable energy could remain a key area of investor interest as expectations of continued federal support for clean-energy development improve sentiment toward solar and other alternative energy companies. Nextpower Inc. NXT, operating in the clean and renewable energy sector, gained 11.1% on Nov. 4 following the election results, reflecting investors' expectations regarding the future policy environment. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy).

Story Continues

Healthcare is another sector to watch, particularly managed-care providers and health insurers with exposure to Medicaid and Affordable Care Act coverage. Potential changes to healthcare funding and coverage policies could influence enrollment, reimbursement and medical costs. Centene CNC, a national healthcare services company, gained 12.6% following the election results. The stock carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). However, Morgan Stanley noted that a divided government could limit the scope of major legislative changes, making the actual impact on healthcare spending uncertain.

AI infrastructure presents a differentiated investment opportunity, as growing data-center demand is accompanied by increasing scrutiny of electricity consumption, water availability, construction permits and project economics. While smaller data-center operators faced selling pressure following the election results, hyperscalers such as Microsoft and Amazon gained more than 6% at yesterday's close. Both stocks currently carry a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank stocks here .

Meta President Dina Powell McCormick said at the Wall Street Journal Tech conference that many different factors contributed to Democrats' election victories, but data-center opposition was clearly one of them. news.Title: Arm Holdings' Q2 Earnings Call Centers on AGI CPU Expansion
news.Content:
Arm Holdings plc ARM highlighted stronger AGI CPU demand on its second-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call, backed by customer orders and supply commitments. Management also emphasized data center adoption.

The company reported revenues of $1.44 billion compared with the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1.37 billion. Non-GAAP earnings of $0.52 per share topped the $0.48 estimate, underpinning its expansion plans.

ARM Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

ARM Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | ARM Holdings PLC Sponsored ADR Quote

Arm Sees Greater AGI CPU Revenue Potential

CEO Rene Haas said that customer orders and improved supply have strengthened confidence in generating up to $2 billion of AGI CPU revenues across fiscal 2027 and 2028. Shipments are targeted for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027.

Responding to StoneX, Haas identified Meta as the principal customer but confirmed additional buyers. Securing wafers, substrates, testing capacity and memory remains critical to deliveries.

CFO Jason Child told Susquehanna that third-quarter shipments would be minimal, if any. Answering Wells Fargo, Child projected first-generation AGI CPU gross margins around 30%-40%, with a longer-term target above 50% on later designs. Haas cited some pricing flexibility to offset higher component costs.

ARM Expects Data Center Share Gains to Continue

Haas said that Arm-based servers held more than 50% market share at top hyperscalers in calendar 2025, up from 15% in 2024. He expects that share to exceed 60% by the end of 2026.

Data center royalties doubled year over year, with management anticipating triple-digit growth in coming years. Haas cited Amazon, Google, Microsoft and NVIDIA as leading contributors, alongside Oracle's plan to offer AGI CPU instances in 2027.

A William Blair analyst pressed Haas on competition with x86 processors. Haas stressed system efficiency and design flexibility, clarifying that its AGI CPU benchmark compared against an AMD processor preceding the newer Venice generation.

Arm's Licensing Pipeline Supports Future Royalties

Child said that license and other revenues rose 50% year over year to $773 million, about $100 million above management's forecast, as customers accelerated longer-term commitments. The SoftBank agreement contributed $209 million.

The quarter included three new Arm Total Access agreements and four compute subsystem licenses, split between data center and smartphone applications. Active Total Access subscriptions exceeded 60, supporting future royalty opportunities.

Story Continues

Asked by Morgan Stanley whether the higher licensing level was sustainable, Child declined to establish a new quarterly baseline. He described a stronger-than-expected pipeline and said agreements can produce royalties within 12 to 24 months.

ARM Sees Contrasting Trends Beyond the Cloud

Child said that edge AI royalties were roughly flat year over year as higher memory prices pressured lower- and midrange smartphone shipments. Higher Armv9 and subsystem royalty rates offset weaker volumes.

In response to Bank of America, Child said that smartphone unit expectations for next year were broadly flat. Nevertheless, he anticipated at least double-digit growth in Arm's mobile business, supported by further adoption of higher-value technology.

Physical AI royalties grew 50% year over year, driven by automotive and robotics demand. Haas highlighted Arm Total Design for physical AI, involving more than 80 companies.

Arm Details Q3 Expectations and Investment Priorities

For third-quarter fiscal 2027, Child projected revenues of $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million, and non-GAAP earnings of 56 cents per share, plus or minus four cents.

He expects licensing revenue growth of slightly more than 50% year over year. Royalties are expected to rise by low teens sequentially but grow only low single digits year over year, with cloud and physical AI strength offset by smartphone weakness.

Non-GAAP operating expenses are projected at approximately $825 million as engineering investment continues. Last quarter, expenses rose 19% to $774 million, while the non-GAAP operating margin reached 44.2%.

ARM Keeps Two Business Models in View

Haas framed ARM's direction around two complementary businesses: licensing intellectual property to chip designers and selling its own AGI CPU silicon. Both share its architecture and developer ecosystem.

Management's priorities remain expanding silicon supply, deepening licensing relationships and sustaining research investment. Memory costs and smartphone demand remain constraints.

What ARM's Zacks Rank and Style Scores Indicate

ARM carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) at present, a neutral near-term rating. Its Growth Score of A and Momentum Score of A indicate favorable traits, while its Value Score of F indicates weaker valuation appeal. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

Its VGM Score of C trails the A or B scores preferred in Zacks' screening framework. The Zacks Rank may change as analyst earnings estimates are revised following the latest results.

news.Title: Nasdaq Futures Slip as Chip Selloff Rages On; Earnings and Fed Speak on Tap
news.Content:
December Nasdaq 100 E-Mini futures (NQZ26) are down -0.67% this morning as investors continued to dump chipmakers and other AI-related stocks following the Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections.

Chip and AI infrastructure stocks slid in pre-market trading, extending yesterday's slump amid concerns that the Democrats' election sweep could bring tighter U.S. data center regulations and weaken demand. Adding to the pressure, Qualcomm (QCOM) plunged more than -8% after issuing soft FQ1 adjusted EPS guidance, while Arm Holdings (ARM) fell over -5% as its FQ3 revenue forecast disappointed investors.

More News from Barchart

Meanwhile, December S&P 500 E-Mini futures (ESZ26) and December Dow Mini futures (YMZ26) advanced, signaling further gains for the benchmarks after their post-election rally.

WTI crude prices edged higher on Thursday, stabilizing after a sharp drop in the previous session. Still, the U.S. benchmark hovered near two-month lows amid speculation that the Democratic sweep could speed up efforts to end the Middle East conflict. Treasuries were mixed.

Looking ahead, investors are awaiting a new wave of U.S. economic data and corporate earnings reports, along with remarks from Federal Reserve officials.

In yesterday's trading session, Wall Street's three main equity benchmarks ended sharply higher as oil prices plunged and investors wagered that a divided government in Washington would benefit stocks. Most members of the Magnificent Seven rallied, with Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon.com (AMZN) climbing over +6%. Also, healthcare stocks popped amid speculation that the Democratic-controlled Congress could reverse the Medicaid cuts included in last year's tax and spending bill, with Centene (CNC) jumping over +12% and HCA Healthcare (HCA) surging more than +10%. In addition, Block (XYZ) soared over +15% and was among the top percentage gainers in the S&P 500 after the fintech firm posted upbeat Q3 results and raised its full-year guidance. On the bearish side, chip and AI infrastructure stocks sank, with Sandisk (SNDK) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) plunging over -7%.

Story Continues

Economic data released on Wednesday were mostly better than expected, supporting equities. The ADP National Employment Report showed that U.S. private-sector payrolls rose by 86K in October, stronger than expectations of 67K. Also, the U.S. trade deficit unexpectedly narrowed to -$105.0 billion in September, compared with expectations for a widening to -$107.9 billion. At the same time, the U.S. ISM services index fell to 54.5 in October, slightly below expectations of 54.8, but remained comfortably above the 50 level separating expansion from contraction.

"U.S. stocks are set for gains into year-end as the election removes a source of uncertainty, earnings remain strong, and lackluster investor positioning leaves room for renewed buying," according to Citadel Securities' Scott Rubner.

Third-quarter corporate earnings season continues, with notable companies including ConocoPhillips (COP), Airbnb (ABNB), Monster Beverage (MNST), and Cloudflare (NET) set to report their quarterly results today. According to Bloomberg Intelligence, S&P 500 companies are expected to post an average +31% jump in third-quarter earnings from a year earlier.

On the economic front, investors will be watching U.S. initial jobless claims data, set to be released in a couple of hours. Economists expect applications for U.S. unemployment benefits to come in at 197K in the week ended Oct. 31, compared with 194K in the prior week.

Preliminary U.S. unit labor costs and nonfarm productivity data will also be in focus today. Economists forecast Q3 unit labor costs to rise +0.3% q/q and nonfarm productivity to climb +2.8% q/q, compared with the second-quarter figures of +1.2% q/q and +1.4% q/q, respectively.

In addition, market participants will parse comments from Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan today.

U.S. rate futures are currently pricing in a 79.2% probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike and a 20.8% probability of no rate change at the December FOMC meeting.

In the bond market, the yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note is at 4.88%, down -0.10%.

The Euro Stoxx 50 Index is up +0.48% this morning, extending gains from the previous session that were fueled by the Democrats' sweeping victory in the U.S. midterm elections. Mining stocks led the advance on Thursday, buoyed by higher metal prices and a post-earnings rally in ArcelorMittal shares. Travel and leisure stocks also climbed on hopes that the Democrats' victory in the U.S. midterms could speed up efforts to end the war in Iran, which would drive down oil prices, lower fuel costs, and boost travel demand. In addition, bank stocks advanced. At the same time, defense stocks slid, with Rheinmetall (RHM.D.DX) tumbling over -16% after it cut its full-year sales guidance. Data released on Thursday showed that German monthly factory orders rose in September, partly recovering from August's sharp decline. Separate data showed that French monthly industrial production unexpectedly fell in September. Meanwhile, Norway's Norges Bank kept its benchmark rate unchanged at 4.50% on Thursday, as widely expected, but left the door open to additional rate hikes if inflation stayed elevated. Investor focus now turns to the Bank of England's interest-rate decision. The BOE is widely expected to raise its key rate by 25 basis points to 4.00% later today, which would mark its first hike in more than three years, as policymakers seek to prevent persistently high energy prices from triggering second-round inflation effects. In other corporate news, Air France-KLM (AF.P.DX) surged over +11% after the company posted better-than-expected Q3 operating profit.

Germany's Factory Orders, France's Industrial Production, and Eurozone's PPI data were released today.

The German September Factory Orders rose +4.4% m/m, weaker than expectations of +4.6% m/m.

The French September Industrial Production unexpectedly fell -0.5% m/m, weaker than expectations of +0.3% m/m.

Eurozone September PPI rose +2.5% m/m and +11.1% y/y, compared to expectations of +2.5% m/m and +10.9% y/y.

Asian stock markets today closed mixed. China's Shanghai Composite Index ($CHSC) closed up +0.10%, and Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index ($NKY) closed down -1.79%.

China's Shanghai Composite Index closed slightly higher today, supported by a rotation trade sparked by the U.S. midterm elections. Gold-related stocks rallied on Thursday as the precious metal regained momentum, buoyed by lower oil prices and Treasury yields. Renewables stocks also jumped, extending their rally as investors viewed the Democratic Party's sweep in the U.S. midterms as a positive development for the industry. In addition, semiconductor stocks climbed, bucking a selloff among their regional peers. However, gains in the benchmark index were capped by declines in energy and optical communications stocks. Morningstar analysts said on Thursday that "China and Hong Kong remain relatively attractive" following an October correction. Meanwhile, Hong Kong stocks jumped on Thursday as investors rotated into beaten-down internet giants. Alibaba Group climbed over +8%, while Tencent Holdings surged more than +7%. Elsewhere, Reuters reported on Thursday that flash-memory chipmaker Yangtze Memory Technologies Co. suspended plans for its Shanghai IPO after Beijing tightened approvals for share offerings in the wake of October's stock market rout.

Japan's Nikkei 225 Stock Index closed sharply lower today, dragged down by a steep selloff in the technology sector. Chip and other AI-related stocks cratered on Thursday, tracking an overnight slump in their U.S. peers as investors feared that Democratic control of Congress could bring tighter regulation of data centers. Chip-testing equipment maker Advantest tanked over -14%, memory-chip maker Kioxia Holdings sank more than -13%, and tech investor SoftBank Group fell over -6%, weighing heavily on the Nikkei. At the same time, automobile stocks surged as investors rotated out of tech shares and into consumer-oriented names, with the sector getting an additional boost from a jump in Toyota Motor shares. Toyota Motor popped over +16% after the automaker raised its full-year profit guidance, citing strong demand for its hybrid vehicles. The so-called stock-rotation trade also lifted real estate and healthcare shares. Meanwhile, minutes from the Bank of Japan's September meeting released on Thursday showed that policymakers saw the need to continue raising interest rates, with some signaling the possibility of a faster pace of tightening. Many BOJ board members flagged a growing likelihood that consumer inflation would accelerate starting in early autumn, noting that rising costs were increasingly being passed on to consumers and that price increases were planned for more food and beverage items than in typical years. On the economic front, a survey showed that Japan's services sector grew modestly in October as business activity and new orders both increased at a slightly faster pace. Investor attention now shifts to Japan's September wage data and a speech from BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda, both scheduled for Friday. The Nikkei Volatility Index, which takes into account the implied volatility of Nikkei 225 options, closed up +34.35% at 33.56.

The Japanese October S&P Global Services PMI was revised downward to 51.7 from the preliminary reading of 52.0.

The tech conglomerate was also swept up in broader selling in tech and AI stocks, especially after the U.S. Democrats swept the midterm elections and won majorities in both chambers of Congress.

The Democrats have signaled more regulatory scrutiny towards AI and data centers, with Softbank holding major exposure to the U.S. data center buildout through its massive investment in OpenAI.

news.Title: ARM Holdings PLC (ARM) (Q2 2027) Earnings Call Highlights: Record Revenue, Surging AI ...
news.Content:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus .

Total Revenue: $1.44 billion, up 27% year over year; record Q2 and second-highest quarterly revenue ever.

License and Other Revenue: $773 million, up 50% year over year; record Q2 and second-highest quarter ever; ~$100 million above expectations.

Royalty Revenue: $670 million, up 8% year over year; highest-ever Q2 figure.

Data Center Royalties: Doubled year over year.

Physical AI Royalties: Grew 50% year over year, driven by automotive and robotics.

Edge AI Royalties: Roughly flat year over year amid smartphone unit pressure from higher memory prices.

SoftBank Agreement Contribution: $209 million of license revenue, up 17% year over year.

Annualized Contract Value (ACV): Grew 12% year over year.

Non-GAAP Operating Expense: $774 million, up 19% year over year.

Non-GAAP Operating Income: $638 million, up 37% year over year.

Non-GAAP Operating Margin: 44.2%, up 300 basis points year over year.

Non-GAAP EPS: $0.52, up 33% year over year.

Free Cash Flow: $1.1 billion over trailing 12 months.

Arm AGI CPU Revenue Outlook: Confidence increased to up to $2 billion across fiscal 2027 and 2028; first commercial deliveries on track for fiscal Q4 '27.

Q3 Revenue Guidance: $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million (~24% year-over-year growth at midpoint).

Q3 License and Other Revenue Guidance: Up a little over 50% year over year.

Q3 Royalty Revenue Guidance: Low-teens sequential growth; low-single-digit year-over-year growth.

Q3 Non-GAAP Operating Expense Guidance: Approximately $825 million.

Q3 Non-GAAP EPS Guidance: $0.56, plus or minus $0.04.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 2 Warning Sign with ARM.

Is ARM fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

Release Date: November 04, 2026

For the complete transcript of the earnings call, please refer to the full earnings call transcript .

Positive Points

Record Q2 revenue of $1.44 billion, up 27% year over year, marking the fifth consecutive quarter of over 20% growth.

License and other revenue grew 50% to $773 million, driven by strong demand for Arm's compute platform and new long-term agreements.

Data center royalties doubled year over year, with Arm-based server market share at top hyperscalers exceeding 50% and expected to surpass 60% by end of calendar 2026.

Arm AGI CPU demand is extremely strong, with confidence in achieving up to $2 billion in revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028, supported by secured supply and multiple customer purchase orders.

Non-GAAP EPS increased 33% to $0.52, and free cash flow over the trailing 12 months was $1.1 billion, providing flexibility for continued investment.

Story Continues

Negative Points

Edge AI royalty revenue was roughly flat year over year due to higher memory prices pressuring smartphone unit sales, particularly in mid- and lower-tier segments.

Royalty revenue growth was only 8% year over year, significantly lower than license growth, due to weakness in smartphone demand and a tough year-over-year comparison.

The Arm AGI CPU business is expected to have gross margins in the high-30s to low-40% range for the first version, below the company's long-term target of 50%+.

Supply chain constraints, including wafer, substrate, tester, and memory availability, pose risks to meeting strong demand for the Arm AGI CPU.

Customer concentration in data center royalties is high, with Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and NVIDIA accounting for the majority of royalties, creating dependency risk.

Q & A Highlights

Q : What is driving Arm's increased confidence in achieving up to $2 billion in Arm AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028, and have additional customers beyond Meta been signed? A : CEO Rene Haas said demand is stronger than at the March Arm Everywhere event, with Meta as the chief customer but multiple customers beyond Meta. Confidence has grown because Arm has spent several quarters securing supply across wafers, substrates, testers, and memory, and has signed purchase orders from multiple customers extending through calendar 2027. First commercial deliveries remain on track for fiscal Q4 2027.

Q : How does Arm expect to win versus x86 in the AI data center, given AMD's claims about Venice performance per watt? A : CEO Rene Haas framed the opportunity in two ways: hyperscalers designing custom SoCs gain flexibility to optimize performance per rack, while Arm's AGI CPU offers strong performance per watt and cost efficiency. He cited Signal65 testing showing roughly twice the performance per rack versus AMD EPYC 9755, and said Arm is confident in customer demand and its road map.

Q : What partners are building Arm AGI CPU rack systems, and what will drive the path to $15 billion in AGI CPU revenue by FY31? A : CEO Rene Haas said Supermicro, Lenovo, and ASRock are building racks for deployment at data centers such as OCI. Growth will be driven by rising core counts as agentic workloads scale, with CPUs potentially moving from 128 to 256 to 500-plus cores, which should lift average selling prices. CFO Jason Child noted the prior plan implied about $2 billion a year after FY28 and about $5 billion a year after that, with updated targets likely at the next Arm Everywhere event.

Q : When should investors expect Arm AGI CPU revenue to begin, and how large could data center become as a share of total royalties? A : CFO Jason Child said shipments will start in Q4, with little if any contribution in Q3. On data center mix, he said data center was approaching about 20% of total royalties last year and will not quite reach a third by the end of this year, but will get there sometime soon, with edge royalties flattish this quarter and recovering in Q4.

Q : How concentrated are cloud and AI royalties among customers? A : CEO Rene Haas said Amazon, Google, and Microsoft are the largest contributors, with NVIDIA ramping quickly. He said those four command the majority of data center royalties.

Q : What is the update on the second-generation Arm AGI CPU and the potential to add networking and high-performance I/O? A : CEO Rene Haas declined to disclose the precise schedule but said the market moves on an 18- to 24-month production ramp cadence, implying timing for the follow-on chip. He said Arm is looking at connectivity, I/O, networking, and other system-level capabilities because rack-level performance matters, though nothing could be announced on the call.

Q : Is the $773 million licensing quarter a new structural level, and what types of agreements drove it? A : CFO Jason Child said the vast majority of licensing is Arm Total Access and CSS, with architecture licenses very rare. He said license revenue should step up again in Q3 and Q4, and while he would not call $773 million the new quarterly norm, the pipeline is stronger than expected, with incremental new deals that are hard to forecast and likely to convert into future royalties.

Q : Could higher-core-count AGI CPUs support higher per-core pricing? A : CEO Rene Haas said memory and data center build costs have risen sharply, so Arm is cautious about pushing pricing too hard, but he sees some pricing elasticity on larger, higher-core-count chips and said there is probably some headroom.

Q : If smartphone units remain weak next year, how should investors think about royalty growth? A : CFO Jason Child said industry forecasts point to roughly flat mobile units next year, with memory constraints already reflected and not expected to deteriorate further. He said greater Armv9 adoption, now over 50%, plus growing CSS adoption and higher royalty rates on next-generation CSS should let Arm grow overall royalties at least in the double digits next year.

Q : Does Arm have enough scale to secure supply for the AGI CPU against larger competitors like AMD? A : CEO Rene Haas acknowledged AMD has far more scale and longer-standing supply relationships, but said Arm has decades-long relationships with TSMC and memory vendors such as Micron, Samsung, and SK. He said Arm has been discussing the platform with supply partners for more than a year and views the AGI CPU as a five- to ten-year endeavor requiring deep supply chain relationships.

Q : How should investors think about gross margins as Arm secures more AGI CPU supply at higher cost? A : CEO Rene Haas said memory is the largest cost pressure, with downstream supply chain impacts also weighing on margins, but Arm has demonstrated some pricing elasticity to offset costs. CFO Jason Child said the first AGI CPU version should carry gross margins in the high-30s to low-40% range, with the first version likely a little lower, moving toward the market standard of 50%-plus on later versions.

Q : What is driving the royalty rate per unit trend, and how should investors model it going forward? A : CFO Jason Child said the blended rate will bounce around given more than 10 billion chips shipped in the quarter, with mobile lower and server and physical AI higher. He advised modeling the three segments separately: flattish mobile, strong double-digit server growth with rising core counts and CSS revenue, and physical AI growing about 50%, supporting confidence in triple-digit data center royalty growth over the next few years.
