news.Title: Is Broadcom Stock a Buy After Marvell's $115 Billion Deal?
news.Content:
On Nov. 2, Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) agreed to buy Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ:LITE), a maker of lasers and optical transceivers, in an all-stock deal. The firms put Lumentum's enterprise value (its stock market value plus debt, minus cash) at $115 billion, using both stocks' Oct. 28 closing prices.

Marvell says the combination creates a category leader in artificial intelligence (AI) connectivity -- the chips and optical parts that send data between AI processors.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO) knows the business well. The chip designer sells custom AI accelerators, Ethernet switches, and optical components for AI data centers. But its stock dipped only about 1% on Nov. 2, while Marvell shares slid about 13%.

At roughly $335 as I write, Broadcom stock trades about 30% under its June 2 record close of $481.57. When I last wrote about the company on Oct. 28, with shares near $342, I said I'd consider buying a little at a time.

Does a bigger rival change that?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Marvell is building a bigger rival

Marvell already designs custom AI chips, plus network switches and the electrical and optical interconnect chips that link AI systems together. Lumentum brings high-performance lasers and optical transceivers, along with its own compound semiconductor manufacturing.

Broadcom competes in most of those markets. It designs custom AI accelerators for six customers, including Alphabet's Google and Anthropic. The chips are made for one customer's AI work, as an alternative to general-purpose graphics processing units (GPUs).

Broadcom also sells Tomahawk Ethernet switches. On its fiscal third-quarter earnings call on Sept. 2, CEO Hock Tan said the company had just finished designing Tomahawk 7, which he called the industry's first 200-terabit-per-second Ethernet switch.

And Broadcom makes lasers, too.

"[D]emand for lasers ... is far surpassing supply out there in the industry," Tan said on the call. He added that Broadcom holds "a fairly substantial share of this market."

Put simply, Lumentum's lasers sell into a market where buyers can't currently get enough of them. Sure, shortages like this don't tend to last. But I think it makes the deal more of a long-term threat to Broadcom than a short-term one. A bigger rival could matter more when supply catches up to demand and buyers start shopping harder on price.

Story Continues

Broadcom's AI sales are still accelerating

Showing how far ahead Broadcom's AI business is, its AI semiconductor revenue hit $16.7 billion in fiscal Q3 (the quarter ended Aug. 2), up 221% year over year. Marvell's total revenue for its own quarter ended Aug. 1 was $2.74 billion, or around one-sixth as much.

And Broadcom's AI growth has picked up every quarter this year. AI revenue growth climbed from 106% in fiscal Q1 to 143% in fiscal Q2, then to 221% in fiscal Q3. Management guided for 236% year-over-year growth, to $21.7 billion, in fiscal Q4, which ended Nov. 1.

Broadcom has its own $115 billion number, and it means something else: the company's forecast for AI semiconductor revenue in fiscal 2027, the fiscal year that started this week.

This would double the almost $58 billion Broadcom expected for fiscal 2026. And Tan said on the Sept. 2 call that the company's already locked in the supply to get there.

"Our demand actually exceeds this outlook, and we will work to improve supply," he said.

The deal won't affect that year directly. Marvell expects the acquisition to close in the first half of calendar 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals. So Broadcom's fiscal 2027 will probably be over before the combined company even exists.

Time to buy?

Investors can buy this growth for less than they'd pay for the S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC). Broadcom trades at around 17 times analysts' consensus earnings estimate for fiscal 2027.

This compares to about 18.7 times forward earnings for the S&P 500 overall.

True, Broadcom relies on a few very big AI customers, and a stronger Marvell could offer these customers another place to shop for custom chips and lasers. But this option is probably years away. And Broadcom's AI business is already several times the size of Marvell's whole company.

Ultimately, the deal doesn't change my take on Broadcom. It does make the company's laser and switching sales worth watching more closely once the combined company exists.

Meanwhile, the stock is a bit cheaper than when I last wrote about it, and nothing in the deal affects Broadcom's fiscal 2027 outlook. I'd still consider buying shares at this price.

Non-GAAP operating expenses rose 19% to $774 million as Arm expanded engineering capacity and invested in new platforms and products. Non-GAAP operating income climbed 37% to $638 million, and the non-GAAP operating margin expanded by 3 percentage points to 44.2%.

Arm raises confidence in AGI CPU outlook

Executives said purchase orders from multiple customers and agreements with suppliers have increased their confidence in achieving up to $2 billion in Arm AGI CPU revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028 . Child said Arm had previously expressed increased confidence in achieving more than $1 billion over that period.

First commercial deliveries remain on track for fiscal fourth-quarter 2027. Child said any shipments in the third quarter would not be substantial and that Arm would provide another update with its third-quarter results.

Haas identified Meta as a chief customer but said Arm expects multiple customers beyond Meta. He said demand had exceeded expectations and that the company had been working for several quarters to secure supplies, including wafers, substrates, testers and memory.

Asked about the cost of obtaining additional supply, Haas said rising system costs create margin pressure, but Arm has some flexibility to increase prices. Child said the company expects the first version of the product to have a gross margin in the high-30% to low-40% range, with a longer-term goal of reaching 50% or more as Arm develops expertise and does more work itself.

Data center growth offsets smartphone pressure

Arm's data center royalty revenue doubled year over year as Arm-based CPUs expanded in AI infrastructure and general-purpose cloud workloads, Child said. Physical AI royalty revenue grew 50%, driven by automotive and robotics adoption.

Edge AI royalty revenue was roughly flat, as higher memory prices pressured smartphone unit sales, particularly in mid- and lower-tier devices. Child said higher royalty rates from adoption of Armv9 and compute subsystem technologies offset that headwind. He expects edge AI royalties to reaccelerate as smartphone conditions normalize.

Haas said Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers rose from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in 2025. Based on expected deployments across Google Axion, AWS Graviton, Microsoft Cobalt and NVIDIA platforms, Arm expects that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026.

During the analyst question-and-answer session, Haas and Child expressed confidence that data center royalties could sustain triple-digit growth over the next several years. Haas pointed to market-share gains and the use of Arm CPUs alongside AI accelerators.

For fiscal third-quarter 2027, Arm forecast revenue of $1.54 billion, plus or minus $50 million. The midpoint would represent approximately 24% growth from a year earlier. The company also projected non-GAAP earnings of $0.56 per share, plus or minus $0.04, and non-GAAP operating expenses of approximately $825 million.

Child said Arm expects licensing and other revenue to grow a little over 50% year over year in the third quarter. Royalty revenue is expected to rise by low-single-digit percentages from a year earlier, as strength in cloud and physical AI is offset by weaker smartphone demand and a difficult comparison with the prior-year period.

Rather than manufacturing chips itself, Arm licenses its designs and instruction-set architectures to semiconductor companies and technology manufacturers, which incorporate them into their own products.

news.Title: Arm stock dips as lack of blowout guidance offsets quarterly results
news.Content:
Investing.com -- Arm on Wednesday delivered a quarterly top- and bottom-line beat, but its current-quarter profit and revenue guidance failed to comfortably top expectations.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

U.S.-listed shares of the British chip designer fell more than 3% in premarket trading Thursday.

Arm is a well-known player in the semiconductor market, with its chip designs being used by companies such as Qualcomm, Apple, and Samsung Electronics in graphics processing units (GPUs) in smartphones, and by cloud computing giants and hyperscalers such as Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, and Meta Platforms.

ARM brings in revenue from licensing its technology to these companies and then charging a royalty fee for each product that uses its design.

The British chip designer's technology is used in developing artificial intelligence-focused server chips. The firm earlier this year also said it was expanding its strategy beyond offering intellectual property and compute subsystems to producing silicon products. This included the launch of a new central processing unit (CPU) designed for AI data centers, called Arm AGI CPU.

"AI is driving unprecedented demand for compute across the cloud, devices and autonomous systems, with Arm being the compute platform of choice. Our business is now driven by two areas, both of which are showing rapid growth: The IP business, where partners increase their investment in Arm technology and deploy record numbers of Arm-based silicon, and our new silicon business, where demand for Arm AGI CPU is extremely strong," ARM top boss Rene Haas and finance chief Jason Child said in a letter to shareholders.

HSBC analysts said Arm reiterated its bullish AGI CPU tone bot noted that "server royalties remain a key driver."

"We believe server royalties remain the key earnings catalyst upside with the clearest visibility over the next 12 month given increasing server CPU TAM and Arm market share along with rising CPU core count which increases royalty ASP per chip," they wrote.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

The Cambridge, England-based company's results come at a time when the broader AI trade on Wall Street has been under pressure. Concerns have soared about the massive amounts of debt being issued by companies to fund their AI infrastructure buildouts and whether such spending will ultimately be rewarded with comparable returns.

Story Continues

Chip stocks in particular have been some of the hardest hit by the downturn in sentiment around AI. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index - a key barometer of chip stocks - slumped 15.4% in October. Meanwhile, U.S.-listed shares of Arm tumbled nearly 29% last month.

Against this backdrop, investors have been closely watching quarterly results from chipmakers and chip designers to gauge the demand for AI chips and whether that demand was strong enough to warrant the unprecedented spending on AI.

"Arm continues to gain share across the data center, driven by growing demand for performance and power efficiency as AI infrastructure scales. Data center royalties doubled year over year, and Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers more than tripled—from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in calendar 2025," the company's top executives said in the letter to shareholders.

"Based on current ramps across Google Axion, AWS Graviton, Microsoft Cobalt, and NVIDIA platforms, we expect that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026," they added.

Raymond James analysts said the management's commentary "suggests it is incrementally confident that it has enough supply and customer commitments for the CPU business for up to $2B of sales through the end of FY28, but we opt to remain conservative until we can discern more tangible trends."

Arm said it earned 52 cents per share on an adjusted basis on revenue of $1.44 billion for its fiscal Q2 2027. Analysts had expected an adjusted profit of 47 cents per share on revenue of $1.38 billion.

For its fiscal Q3 2027, ARM sees adjusted profit per share of 56 cents plus/minus 4 cents on revenue of $1.54 billion plus/minus $50 million. The consensus estimates had been for a profit of 55 cents per share on revenue of $1.53 billion.

news.Title: What a $115 Billion Deal to Buy Lumentum Really Means for Marvell Stock Investors
news.Content:
Semiconductor company Marvell Technology (MRVL) is all set to acquire Lumentum (LITE), a leading supplier of optical and photonic technologies, for $115 billion in an all-stock deal. Under the terms of the agreement, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 shares of Marvell for each share of LITE stock they own. Marvell shareholders will own 67% of the combined company, while the rest will be held by Lumentum shareholders.

Marvell investors made their displeasure about the development clear, with shares ending almost 13% lower on Nov. 2 and down again today. They appear to believe the price tag of the deal is too high while the heavy dilution is also undesirable. Notably, the $115 billion consideration is an 86% premium to Lumentum's current market capitalization of $61.6 billion.

More News from Barchart

Why Investors Should Load Up on Google Stock Now

Billionaire Mark Cuban Says the Hardest Part of Fixing Health Costs Isn't the CEOs or Insurance Companies, 'Employees Fight Any Change'

Coca-Cola Pays Warren Buffett's Berkshire $848 Million a Year as Jim Cramer Says Buy KO Stock

Tired of missing midday reversals? The FREE Barchart Brief newsletter keeps you in the know. Sign up now!

However, Marvell management believes that the deal has the potential to result in cost savings of more than $1 billion. "The companies that move first and help define this transition will set the standard for decades to come," said CEO Matt Murphy, describing the artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure market's focus on optical connectivity as a "once in a generation" opportunity. "By bringing together two leaders with highly complementary technologies, exceptional talent and specialized manufacturing capabilities, we intend to help shape the next era of AI connectivity and create exceptional stockholder value."

About Marvell Technology

Founded in 1995, Marvell is an AI infrastructure company centered on data-center connectivity, custom silicon, optical interconnects, switching, and storage. Its custom silicon business in particular includes custom AI accelerators, XPUs, networking chips, storage and memory controllers, and data-center interconnect products. Marvell has an impressive customer base that includes Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), and Alphabet (GOOGL), among others.

Marvell currently commands a market cap of $150.8 billion, with MRVL stock up an impressive 86% on a year-to-date (YTD) basis. Notably, the stock also offers a modest dividend yield of 0.14%.

So, keeping the immediate market reaction aside, how will Marvell's impending acquisition of Lumentum impact its operations? Let's take a closer look.

Story Continues

Lumentum Is Legit for Marvell in the Long Haul

One rationale being bandied about the deal is that Marvell will gain access to Lumentum's expertise in optical transceivers, which allows for faster data transfer with less power. However, Marvell is buying more than faster optical transceivers. The bigger ambition of the deal is to control more of the technology connecting AI processors — from custom silicon and networking chips to lasers, optical modules, and optical circuit switches.

Notably, Marvell wants to design the electrical and optical signal chain together rather than optimize individual components separately. Bringing its silicon photonics, switching, and custom processors together with Lumentum's lasers and optical manufacturing could reduce engineering friction, simplify customer qualification, and shorten development cycles, resulting in the development of a vertically integrated semiconductor player that is harder to replace once its technologies are incorporated into a customer's design.

Meanwhile, Lumentum also brings indium phosphide capabilities and specialized laser production that complement Marvell's semiconductor design strengths. Additionally, optical circuit switching provides a separate growth opportunity beyond transceivers.

On Nov. 2, amid its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results, Lumentum said that optical circuit switch (OCS) demand visibility could support a business generating several billion dollars annually. Management also disclosed a second major win involving optics placed near or alongside processors, supported by purchase commitments exceeding $5 billion. Those commitments give the Marvell acquisition thesis more substance than a broad forecast for rising AI traffic alone.

Finally, with Lumentum, Marvell will be able to offer potential customers a more complete alternative to its larger peer and biggest competitor, Broadcom (AVGO). However, integration also creates a potential channel conflict. Customers that currently buy components from independent suppliers may hesitate if their supplier becomes a broader competitor. Marvell must preserve those relationships while pursuing more integrated sales.

Marvell Reports a Super Q2

Before examining Marvell's Q2 figures, we should look at the company's updated commentary on fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 revenue. Marvell raised its revenue outlook for both years, now projecting fiscal 2027 revenue of $12 billion and fiscal 2028 revenue of $18 billion, up from previous guidance of $11.5 billion and $16.5 billion, respectively. Within the fiscal 2028 outlook, Marvell anticipates data-center revenue growth of 60%, underscoring continued strength in the largest segment of the AI infrastructure buildout.

That momentum was visible in the latest quarterly results as well. Marvell reported record net revenue of $2.74 billion in Q2 fiscal 2027, representing a 37% increase from the prior year. Although that absolute figure set a new high, the growth rate lagged Broadcom, which recorded a 48% rise in its corresponding Q2 results. Meanwhile, Marvell's data-center revenue advanced 46% year-over-year (YOY) to $2.17 billion in Q2.

Gross margins contracted modestly to 58.9% from 59.4% in the year-ago period as stock-based compensation rose to $15.9 million from $13.4 million. Nevertheless, EPS increased 40% YOY to $0.94, just above the consensus estimate of $0.93.

For Q3, Marvell guided EPS between $1.05 and $1.15. Gross margins for Q3 are expected to fall in the range of 57.5% to 58.5%.

Net cash from operating activities improved to $605.5 million from $461.6 million in the prior year. Overall, Marvell closed Q2 with $3.93 billion in cash and no short-term debt. Long-term debt of approximately $5 billion, however, continues to appear as higher interest expense on the income statement. Interest expense rose to $61.6 million from $51.9 million in the same period last year.

Meanwhile, the searing rally in MRVL stock this year has led to punchy valuations. Its forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 56.1 times, price-to-sales (P/S) ratio of 18.3 times, and price-to-cash flow (P/CF) multiple of 47.1 times are all above the sector medians of 21.1 times, 3.2 times, and 18.7 times, respectively.

What Do Analysts Think of MRVL Stock?

Taking all of this into account, analysts have a consensus "Strong Buy" rating for MRVL stock overall. Out of 39 analysts covering the stock, 28 have a "Strong Buy" rating, three have a "Moderate Buy" rating, and eight have a "Hold" rating. The mean target price of $317.05 denotes potential upside of 102% from current levels.

news.Title: Marvell's Deal to Acquire Lumentum Could Be a Game Changer for the Stock
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) has been a big winner this year, with the stock up more than 130% in 2026, as of the end of October. However, an announced deal to acquire Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) could be a game changer for what has already been a good story.

This deal is all about optical networking, as it will combine Marvell's leadership in optical interconnects with Lumentum's strength in lasers. Marvell called the deal a "once-in-a-generation opportunity to define and lead AI connectivity in the era of integrated optics," as it will provide the company with end-to-end design capabilities that will allow it to accelerate its time to market and solve the increasing complexity of scale-up and scale-out networks.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Let's see what this could all mean for investors.

Complementary technologies

The two companies' optics technologies are very complementary. In an optical network, Marvell provides electronic components such as DSPs (digital signal processors) that prepare data to be converted into optical signals; transimpedance amplifiers (TIAs) that convert light signals back into electrical signals; and silicon photonics (SiPho) engines that combine hundreds of components to improve the performance and energy efficiency of optical interconnects.

Lumentum produces high-power indium phosphide (InP) lasers and gallium arsenide (GaAs) vertical cavity surface-emitting lasers (VCSELs) that convert electricity into light for high-speed data transmission. It is one of a handful of companies with this technology for these advanced lasers. Designing and manufacturing these lasers is a complex task, and the company holds over 1,000 patents and owns specialized semiconductor fabs (manufacturing facilities).

Marvell said that the acquisition will allow it to go from producing components to full modules. It will also create meaningful design and operational efficiencies for its customers. It believes that integrating its technology with Lumentum is ultimately needed to take bandwidth, latency, and power efficiency to the next level.

The deal will combine what are expected to be two of the S&P 500 's fastest-growing companies by earnings per share (EPS) from 2026 through 2028. Meanwhile, Marvell believes its combined total addressable market (TAM) will be around $550 billion by 2030. It sees $1 billion in potential annual synergies with the deal, largely coming from a reduction in cost of goods sold. Excluding synergies, the company will have a $17.7 billion annual revenue run rate with 57% gross margins and 39% operating margins .

Story Continues

As part of the deal, Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each share they own. The deal valued Lumentum at an enterprise value of $115 billion, or about $1,132 per share, at the time of the announcement. That represents about a 24% premium to its closing price before the announcement. The deal is expected to close in the first half of calendar 2028.

Time to buy the stocks

Both Marvell and Lumentum have been riding the shift in AI data centers from copper wire to optical networks, which offer better bandwidth and lower energy costs. As AI innovation continues to advance and systems become more powerful, the need for optical networking should only grow.

Both companies are already seeing strong growth individually. Lumentum reported its fiscal first-quarter results the same day as the merger announcement. It grew its revenue by 137% to $1.26 billion, while its gross margins climbed 1,700 basis points to 51%. Meanwhile, Marvell had guided for its current quarter revenue to increase by 52%, with data center revenue surging 75%. The combined company will become a juggernaut in the optical space.

Marvell is more than optics, though, as it is also a leader in custom AI chips. It provides important IP (intellectual property) for both Amazon 's AI Trainium chips and Microsoft 's newer Maia chips. It also recently won a deal to supply Alphabet 's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) architecture with important attach components, such as inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute.

Marvell's pending acquisition of Lumentum, plus its strength in custom AI chips, gives Marvell one of the best long-term growth outlooks in the AI infrastructure space. That makes the AI stock a buy, with Lumentum being a discounted way to own Marvell -- although there is always some risk that a deal may not go through.

news.Title: Marvell Stock Has Plunged 46% Since Jensen Huang Called It the Next $1 Trillion Company. Here's Why.
news.Content:
In early June, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang called Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) the next trillion-dollar company. Huang explained that Marvell's connectivity solutions are essential for coordinating large clusters of processors powering artificial intelligence (AI) systems.

Wall Street initially embraced this optimism. Marvell shares surged to about $291 on June 2 and reached a record closing price of nearly $316 just two days later. However, enthusiasm around Marvell seems to have evaporated. As of Nov. 2, Marvell stock traded at $171, representing a decline of 46% from its peak.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

MRVL data by YCharts

The sell-off follows Marvell's announcement that it is acquiring optical networking specialist Lumentum (NASDAQ: LITE) in a $115 billion deal . Let's unpack why Wall Street is reacting so negatively to this news and assess whether investors are overlooking the long-term opportunity.

Why Jensen Huang sees trillion-dollar potential in Marvell

Marvell is quietly becoming an important supplier to the AI infrastructure supercycle. The company's custom application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) allow hyperscalers to build processors optimized for particular training and inference workloads, while its networking and connectivity products help transfer information between chips and servers.

Nvidia recognized this opportunity early on, announcing a $2 billion investment in Marvell and a partnership involving its NVLink Fusion platform. The collaboration allows AI developers to combine custom silicon designed by Marvell with Nvidia's broader computing and networking architectures.

Why the Lumentum acquisition sent Marvell stock plunging

On Nov. 2, Marvell announced an agreement to acquire Lumentum in an all-stock transaction carrying an implied enterprise value of approximately $115 billion. The acquisition values Lumentum at approximately $1,132 per share, representing a 24% premium to its closing price on Oct. 28, right as speculation about the deal surfaced.

The transaction's structure is important to understand. Rather than paying cash or taking on debt to finance the acquisition, Marvell will issue 4.5 new shares for every outstanding Lumentum share. Following the transaction, Marvell shareholders will own 67% of the combined company while Lumentum shareholders will control the remaining 33%.

Story Continues

This means Marvell's investors are effectively surrendering one-third of the combined company's ownership to acquire Lumentum. That dilution explains Wall Street's negative reaction. However, since the agreement uses a fixed exchange ratio rather than a guaranteed cash price, the value Lumentum shareholders ultimately receive will fluctuate with Marvell's stock price. In other words, the acquisition's headline valuation isn't necessarily the price Marvell will actually pay.

Is Wall Street overlooking Marvell's long-term potential?

Despite the dilution, I think there are some meaningful benefits to this deal. Marvell's portfolio includes digital signal processors (DSPs), networking chips, and connectivity solutions that enable data to move through AI systems. Lumentum complements those capabilities with lasers and optical components used to transmit information at low latencies. Combining these solutions allows Marvell to offer customers a more complete optical connectivity suite.

Management expects the transaction to generate more than $1 billion in annual run rate cost synergies and become accretive to adjusted earnings per share (EPS) during the first year post-close.

Although the market's reaction has been severe so far, investors should not lose sight of Marvell's long-term potential. During its investor day last month, management estimated that its total addressable market (TAM) could reach $400 billion by calendar 2030. Following the proposed Lumentum acquisition, the combined company's addressable market is expected to expand to $550 billion.

Another important development involves Alphabet . In August, Marvell disclosed an agreement to develop custom semiconductors supporting Google's Tensor Processing Unit (TPU) ecosystem. As part of the arrangement, Google received warrants to purchase 59 million Marvell shares at $206.58 each.

I think the agreements with Google and Nvidia reinforce Marvell's rising position as an important partner to some of the world's largest AI infrastructure customers. Ultimately, Marvell's acquisition of Lumentum could strengthen its competitive position by bridging optical components and semiconductor design under one roof.

Nevertheless, the market seems to be focusing on what existing shareholders need to give up in the short term. Huang's trillion-dollar prediction remains ambitious, but the strategic rationale behind his enthusiasm hasn't disappeared just because Marvell's stock price is falling.

For investors willing to tolerate volatility in the near term and wait a few years for the acquisition's benefits to materialize in both revenue and profit, Marvell's sell-off could represent an attractive opportunity to buy the dip.

news.Title: 3 Reasons to Hold Amkor Stock Despite Its High Premium P/E
news.Content:
Amkor Technology AMKR is gaining traction in advanced semiconductor packaging for artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing and automotive electronics. However, its valuation premium, recent share-price weakness and falling earnings estimates suggest investors should resist chasing the stock. While its long-term growth opportunities support retaining existing positions, near-term execution risks and substantial capital requirements warrant a measured approach.

AMKR's Premium Valuation Warrants Patience

Amkor trades at 14.62X forward 12-month earnings compared with 8.87X for the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry, a premium of approximately 62%. Although the stock remains below its one-year median P/E of 27.77X, its current valuation already reflects optimism surrounding advanced packaging and AI-related demand. Nevertheless, downward earnings estimate revisions and moderating growth expectations raise concerns about the sustainability of this premium. Its Value Score of A reflects favorable valuation metrics under the Zacks framework.

AMKR's P/E F12M Ratio

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AMKR Stock Lags Industry and Key Peers

Over the past three months, AMKR's shares declined 30.2%, underperforming the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's 18.1% loss and the Computer and Technology sector's 7.7% fall.

AMKR's recent share-price performance also stands out against its peers, including ASE Technology Holding ASX, Entegris ENTG and Synaptics SYNA. Over the past three months, ASE Technology Holding's shares gained 6.1%, Entegris returned 4.9% and Synaptics appreciated 17.2%. The stronger performance of ASE Technology Holding, Entegris and Synaptics, despite their different business models and semiconductor industry exposures, highlights relatively weaker investor sentiment toward Amkor.

Three-Months Price Comparison

AI and Data Center Packaging Could Sustain Growth

Third-quarter 2026 Computing revenues increased 37% year over year and 25% sequentially to a record, helped by the ramp of Amkor's flagship high-density fan-out (HDFO) CPU program. Another hyperscaler HDFO CPU program began ramping in the quarter, while two 2.5D networking and data center programs were expected to come online in the fourth quarter. Management anticipates more than 50% year-over-year Computing growth in the fourth quarter.

Management also indicated that Computing revenues could grow more than 30% in 2026, with a similar or higher growth rate possible in 2027. These programs broaden Amkor's AI infrastructure opportunity and provide a potential multiyear growth driver. Its expanding HDFO and 2.5D capabilities could also strengthen its competitive positioning against companies such as ASE Technology Holding. Growing demand for advanced packaging could enable Amkor to capture a larger share of AI infrastructure spending and diversify its revenue base.

Story Continues

Richer Product Mix Is Improving Profitability

Third-quarter net sales were nearly flat year over year at $1.99 billion, but earnings rose to 76 cents from 51 cents per share. Gross margin expanded 400 basis points to 18.3%, while operating margin improved to 11.3% from 8% a year earlier. Management attributed gross margin expansion primarily to a richer mix of high-value advanced packaging, including products with lower material content.

Automotive and Industrial revenues advanced 37% year over year, supported by demand for advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS), in-car computing and industrial products. This mix shift supports earnings resilience even as Communications remains exposed to smartphone demand. Communications accounted for 37% of quarterly sales, down from 51% a year earlier, while Computing increased its contribution to 26% from 19%.

The improving contribution from Computing and Automotive and Industrial provides evidence that Amkor is gradually diversifying beyond its traditional Communications exposure. A richer advanced-packaging mix and stronger contributions from higher-growth end markets could support further margin improvement. Nevertheless, component shortages and changes in customer production schedules remain potential constraints.

Customer Commitments Support Capacity Expansion

Amkor's long-term customer relationships and advance-payment arrangements provide greater visibility into future demand and help support its capacity expansion. Management stated that the company had executed advance-payment arrangements with a dozen customers since 2025, primarily supporting advanced-packaging capacity in Korea and Arizona.

Additionally, an October 2026 customer agreement is expected to provide approximately $1.3 billion in advance payments during 2027. These arrangements should help fund planned investments and reduce some of the near-term financing burden.

Phase 1 of the Arizona advanced-packaging and test campus is scheduled for completion by the end of 2027, while Phase 2 is expected to break ground in late 2027. Together, the two phases represent an estimated investment of $12 billion. The expansion, alongside ongoing investments in Korea and Vietnam, should strengthen Amkor's geographic footprint and ability to serve customers seeking advanced packaging and test capabilities.

Near-Term Outlook and Spending Remain Challenging

For fourth-quarter 2026, Amkor expects revenues of $1.9-$2 billion, gross margin of 18%-19% and earnings of 65-75 cents per share. Communications weakness, component shortages and the system-in-package migration from South Korea to Vietnam remain headwinds. Full-year capital expenditures are projected near $2.5 billion, with higher spending expected in 2027. Free cash flow was negative $319 million in the first nine months of 2026, versus negative $13 million a year earlier. At September-end, cash and short-term investments of $2.4 billion roughly matched total debt of $2.5 billion, while the top 10 customers accounted for 66% of third-quarter sales. This concentration makes disciplined execution important.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for fourth-quarter 2026 earnings per share (EPS) fell to 71 cents from 80 cents over the past 30 days. The first-quarter 2027 EPS estimate fell to 49 cents from 57 cents. The full-year 2026 EPS estimate declined to $2.50 from $2.60, while the 2027 estimate slipped to $2.59 from $2.72.

Conclusion

Amkor's expanding advanced-packaging pipeline, improving product mix and longer-term customer commitments provide sound reasons for existing investors to stay invested rather than sell after the pullback. However, the premium forward P/E, negative free cash flow, smartphone exposure and downward earnings revisions limit the case for aggressive buying.

Investors can hold AMKR while monitoring HDFO and 2.5D program execution, capacity utilization and a recovery in earnings estimates. A sustained improvement in free cash flow and evidence that new capacity can generate attractive returns would further strengthen the investment case. New buyers may prefer clearer evidence that heavy investments will translate into sustainable cash generation.

AMKR currently has a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: How to Play the Selloff in Arm Stock
news.Content:
The recent tech selloff has been especially tough on semiconductor stocks, with Arm Holdings (ARM) suffering the most. Shares fell more than 11% during the Friday trading session on Oct. 30, before recovering somewhat to end down by around 10%. The selling sentiment continued on Monday, though ARM had been bouncing back to around $203.71 during Tuesday's session before dropping again as trading kicked off Wednesday morning.

Importantly, the decline wasn't caused by poor earnings results from Arm itself. Rather, concerns over returns from investments in AI infrastructure have been putting a lot of pressure on the overall semiconductor group. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), Nvidia (NVDA), and Broadcom (AVGO) have all seen significant declines. Nevertheless, with Arm set to report earnings on Nov. 4, there are additional reasons to rethink the company's valuation and prospects for growth.

More News from Barchart

Why Investors Should Load Up on Google Stock Now

Billionaire Mark Cuban Says the Hardest Part of Fixing Health Costs Isn't the CEOs or Insurance Companies, 'Employees Fight Any Change'

Dear Qualcomm Stock Fans, Mark Your Calendars for November 4

Stop Missing Market Moves: Get the FREE Barchart Brief – your midday dose of stock movers, trending sectors, and actionable trade ideas, delivered right to your inbox. Sign Up Now!

About Arm Stock

Based in Cambridge, England, Arm Holdings develops and licenses semiconductor IP, including energy-efficient CPU architectures that are used in a wide array of applications ranging from smartphones and data centers to automotive systems and AI devices. Instead of selling chips itself, Arm makes its money mostly from licensing and royalties; however, the recent move into producing its own silicon has changed that somewhat. At Monday's close, the company had a market cap of around $210 billion.

Although the company has seen a noticeable correction, ARM stock has performed well this year. Shares have been up by around 86% year-to-date (YTD), easily outperforming the 12% gain in the Nasdaq-100 Index. Nevertheless, the stock has lost about 34% over the past month and currently sits at around 55% below its 52-week high of $452.70.

The most serious concern right now is valuation. ARM trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 178.76x and a P/S ratio of 44.71x. In contrast, a peer group valuation dataset for semiconductors puts the median price-to-sales (P/S) ratio at around 14.6x.

Therefore, even despite this steep selloff, Arm still looks expensive. Investors are paying a very high price for the company's exposure to AI infrastructure and for its ability to generate more revenue per generation of chips.

Story Continues

Beats on Earnings as AI Demand Accelerates

The recent earnings results of Arm provide quite a different story compared to the recent price performance. During the July 29 conference call, the company reported Q1 2027 earnings that beat expectations on both top and bottom lines. Revenue came in at $1.29 billion, rising 22% year-over-year (YoY) and beating Wall Street's expectation of approximately $1.26 billion. EPS was $0.45, above the consensus of $0.40 and up 29% from the year before.

What attracted my attention was the performance of Arm's royalty business, which saw its revenue rise by 22% to $715 million, while licensing revenue increased 23% to $574 million. Importantly, data center royalties have grown more than two times YoY, implying that Arm is now benefiting more and more from the transition to power-efficient AI infrastructure.

Moreover, Arm's newly introduced AGI CPU provides another opportunity. According to management, the demand for the product from customers now exceeds $2 billion over fiscal years 2027 and 2028, compared to the previously mentioned initial $1 billion opportunity. However, it shouldn't be confused with actual revenue recognition, since the company is still struggling with increasing manufacturing capacity.

There are also some worries. While reporting robust revenue growth, the company's GAAP operating income decreased by approximately 20% YoY to $91 million. That was due to higher operating expenses and investments in R&D. With Arm moving beyond its traditional licensing business model, execution and profitability have now become more and more important.

Looking forward, the company guided Q2 revenue to be around $1.38 billion, ±$50 million, and EPS to be $0.47, ±$0.04. Wall Street expects the company to bring in approximately $1.38 billion in revenue and earn $0.48 in EPS, meaning that analysts expect another quarter of double-digit revenue growth.

It has been confirmed that Arm will publish its Q2 2027 results on Wednesday, Nov. 4, after the market close. Given the recent volatility, the upcoming earnings report may be quite critical for determining whether shares stabilize or suffer another correction.

What Do Analysts Expect From ARM Stock?

Despite the sharp drop, Wall Street has remained fairly optimistic about Arm's outlook. Analysts assign ARM stock a "Moderate Buy" rating consensus with a mean price target of $289.14. Based on the recent price of $199, its mean target implies a potential upside of approximately 47%. At the same time, the highest price target of $480 implies a potential upside of approximately 136%, while the lowest target of $130 offers a potential downside of roughly 34%. This rather large range reflects the uncertainty concerning Arm's earnings potential and its valuation.

news.Title: MRVL Plunges 36% in a Month: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold the Stock?
news.Content:
Marvell Technology MRVL shares have lost 35.9% in the past month compared with the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry and the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's decline of 22% and 14.1%, respectively.

MRVL One-Month Performance Chart

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Despite the downward movement in MRVL's stock price, MRVL has remained at a premium valuation. MRVL stock is trading at a P/S multiple of 8.58X, much higher than the industry's multiple of 3.08X. The premium valuation is further substantiated by a Zacks Value Score of F.

MRVL Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Given the dynamics, investors must be wondering if it's the right time to invest, retain or sell the stock. Let's discuss the fundamentals of the company to get a better insight.

MRVL Stock Faces a Temporary Setback Amid Long-Term AI Growth

The decline in MRVL's stock price has come amid a broader sell-off in AI-related stocks spanning hyperscalers, semiconductor companies and AI infrastructure providers, as investors increasingly question whether massive AI investments will generate sufficient returns. Since MRVL supplies its solutions to these infrastructure providers, MRVL's stock has also been affected.

Marvell's recent stock decline coincides with the announcement of its proposed $115 billion acquisition of Lumentum Holdings LITE. Under the terms of the all-stock deal, Lumentum stockholders will receive a fixed exchange ratio of 4.5 shares of Marvell common stock for each Lumentum share held, raising investor concerns over valuation, shareholder dilution and the transaction's potential impact on earnings.

However, in the long term, the acquisition of Lumentum will add a substantial portfolio of optical and photonic technologies used in AI data centers, cloud infrastructure, telecommunications networks and advanced manufacturing. Lumentum's Optical Circuit Switching, high-speed transceivers and laser components are of the most strategic importance for MRVL.

Marvell's accelerating AI-driven growth provides a favorable backdrop for its proposed acquisition of Lumentum. Marvell's second-quarter fiscal 2027 revenues increased 37% year over year to $2.74 billion, led by a 46% increase in data-center revenues to $2.17 billion, which accounted for 79% of total sales. Management raised its fiscal 2027 revenue growth outlook to approximately 45%, or roughly $12 billion, while expecting data-center revenues to increase about 60%, up from its prior expectation of approximately 50%.

Story Continues

Within Marvell's portfolio, custom silicon is emerging as an increasingly important growth driver as hyperscalers expand their demand for specialized XPUs and XPU-attach products. AI connectivity also remains strong, with demand for 800G optical DSPs continuing and 1.6T products ramping rapidly. Marvell's scale-out switching business is on track to more than double in fiscal 2027, driven by growing adoption of 51.2T switches across a broader customer base. Meanwhile, increasing customer interest in scale-up optics and switching solutions could provide additional growth opportunities as AI infrastructure architectures evolve.

MRVL to Benefit From a Broader Portfolio

The integration of MRVL's electrical and optical interconnect, switching and custom silicon technologies with Lumentum's high-performance lasers, optical transceivers and optical circuit switching capabilities is expected to create a comprehensive connectivity portfolio spanning scale-across, scale-out, scale-up and scale-in architectures. These factors will strengthen MRVL's competitive positioning relative to Broadcom AVGO and enhance its ability to compete with Coherent COHR.

Broadcom is a leader in the domain of custom silicon solutions for data centers. Broadcom's advanced 3.5D XDSiP packaging platform is critical to ensure the performance and efficiency of custom AI XPUs. Combining Marvell's custom silicon, switching and DSP technologies with Lumentum's lasers, transceivers and optical switching could help MRVL compete with Broadcom's integrated AI connectivity portfolio.

Coherent is a vertically integrated manufacturer of lasers, transceivers, optoelectronic devices and modules and engineered materials that serve communications, industrial, instrumentation and electronics markets. Lumentum's optical components and laser technologies would strengthen MRVL's optical portfolio, enabling it to compete more effectively with Coherent in high-performance lasers and optical connectivity.

Amid these developments, investors need to keep a close eye on Marvell's ability to translate the acquisition of Lumentum into meaningful competitive gains. MRVL's profitability remains sensitive to product mix as newer data center platforms ramp up. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for MRVL's fiscal 2027 earnings is pegged at $4.21 per share, implying year-over-year growth of 48%. Estimates have remained unchanged for the past 30 days.

Conclusion

The recent decline in Marvell's stock price may present an opportunity for investors seeking exposure to the expanding AI infrastructure market. MRVL's strengths in custom silicon, optical connectivity, switching and data-center interconnect, along with its proposed acquisition of Lumentum, could support its long-term growth prospects.

However, the proposed acquisition also introduces integration, shareholder dilution and execution risks. Investors should closely monitor the transaction's progress, MRVL's profitability trends and the company's ability to translate its expanding portfolio into sustainable earnings growth.

news.Title: Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights: QQQ, CoreWeave, SanDisk, Marvell, Arm and Micron
news.Content:
For Immediate Release

Chicago, IL – November 4, 2026– Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Nasdaq 100 Index QQQ, CoreWeave CRWV, SanDisk SNDK, Marvell MRVL, Arm Holdings ARM and Micron MU.

Q4 QQQ Roadmap: Navigating AI Turbulence & Market Headwinds

2026 Stock Market Review

Here is a roadmap of what has occurred with the Nasdaq 100 Index in 2026.

Overall, there are 3 major takeaways:

1)      The market continues to climb the proverbial wall of worry. If I had told you oil and rates are where they are, and the market has held up this well, few would have believed me.

2)      The market and the economy depend heavily AI. The slightest concern of AI infrastructure spending slowing sends stocks crashing.

3)      Market indices don't tell the full story.

Tech Destruction

Last year, investors complained that tech was holding up the market; now the narrative has flipped. QQQ just suffered its worst 3-day decline since "Liberation Day." Meanwhile, according to Morgan Stanley, U.S. tech momentum, or the lack of it, has been worse than the dot-com bust.

What is Holding Back the Equity Market?

· Inflation/Higher Interest Rates

· AI Political Headwinds

· AI Funding/Debt Fears

· Gravity/Profit Taking

Below I explain why the market will overcome these hurdles in the coming months:

Inflation & Higher Rates

Higher energy prices have led to inflation concerns and higher interest rates. That said, geopolitical energy shocks are often short-lived. Tuesday, energy prices fell sharply after Al-Araby Al-Jadeed reported progress toward a US–Iran agreement involving nuclear concessions and frozen funds.

The latest projections lean heavily toward 3 to 4 rate hikes (25 bps increments) over the path extending into mid-to-late 2027. According to BlueKurtic Market Insights (@BlueKurtic), the data shows that equities can perform well during rate-hiking cycles, especially if the pace is measured. This looks like a non-cyclical hike, with no more than 2-3 hikes. This scenario usually hasn't been bad for stocks. The last non-cyclical hike was in 1997, and the S&P 500 gained 40% over the next year, outperforming longer hiking cycles.

Midterm Election Impact: Gridlock is Good

According to a Reuters Poll, only a third of Americans approve of the fast pace of data-center construction. In my view, the stock market has been pricing in a Democratic "Blue Wave" for a few months now, and that is part of why we have seen carnage in AI stocks. Nevertheless, the stock market during periods of divided government has "typically exceeded returns achieved when one political party controls the White House, Senate, and House of Representatives."

Story Continues

The stock market has been pricing in a "Blue Wave" for a few months now, and that is part of the reasons we have seen carnage in AI stocks. In other words, because the market is a forward discounting mechanism, I believe it will result in a classic "sell the rumor, buy the news" situation. Seasonality data backs this notion up. The S&P 500 has finished higher in the six months following every midterm election since 1950. That's 19 consecutive elections with an average gain of nearly 15% regardless of which party came out on top.

AI Debt/Funding Fears

CoreWeave shares plunged in October after its bond yields jumped to distressed levels. Although CoreWeave is plagued by high-debt levels, the market has been acting as if it will go bankrupt. However, betting markets suggest that won't happen any time soon. In September, PolyMarket priced a 2027 CoreWeave bankruptcy as high as 50%. Today, that number is just 12%.

Tech Stock Gravity & Profit Taking

Earlier this year, many AI-related names went too far, too fast. For example, SanDisk blew past the 4.236% bull flag Fibonacci extension by a lot (highly unusual and very rare) and jumped 4,000% in a year. Also, shares were 264% above the 200-day. Typically, a stock 200% above the 200-day is very extreme. In other words, AI stocks got too far ahead of themselves. I think of the 200-day MA as a bungee cord. If it gets too far, it pulls you back in. However, even the strongest stocks retreat to the 200-day. Now, I believe it has overshot. The first touch is often a fantastic area. We are seeing this across many AI stocks including, Marvell , Arm Holdings , Micron and many others.

Bottom Line

While headline fears around AI leverage, interest rates, and political shifts have triggered sharp sector rotation, the market's technical foundation remains intact. Extended growth leaders are completing necessary mean-reversion pullbacks to major moving averages, clearing out leverage while forward-looking indicators point to a classic post-midterm rally. As historical seasonality and political gridlock align with favorable risk-reward entries across core infrastructure names, the current pullback presents a compelling backdrop for the next leg higher.

Research Chief Names "Single Best Pick to Double"

From thousands of stocks, 5 Zacks experts each have chosen their favorite to skyrocket +100% or more in months to come. From those 5, Director of Research Sheraz Mian hand-picks one to have the most explosive upside of all.

This company targets millennial and Gen Z audiences, generating nearly $1 billion in revenue last quarter alone. A recent pullback makes now an ideal time to jump aboard. Of course, all our elite picks aren't winners but this one could far surpass earlier Zacks' Stocks Set to Double like Nano-X Imaging which shot up +129.6% in little more than 9 months.

news.Title: 華邦電賺翻股價卻跌停？  專家喊「派對未結束」 大摩最新目標價出爐
news.Content:
記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）近日公布第三季財，EPS高達7.58元，前三季累計 15.32元，毛利率更衝上70.6%，不過股民並未買單，華邦電3日股價連慘遭打入跌停，今（4）日更是觸及132.5元波段新低，連兩日累積跌幅超過16%。

對此，投資專家「股人阿勳」分析，市場不買單的理由是「記憶體漲價太兇」，就連蘋果都開始承受不了成本壓力，必須透過調漲產品售價轉嫁消費者，一旦終端需求受到影響，上游記憶體的拉貨動能自然可能放緩。

股人阿勳補充，雖然這個擔憂有道理，但現在宣布派對結束恐怕還太早，畢竟華邦電也在法說提到，記憶體供給仍然吃緊，甚至預期2027年可能比今年更缺貨。

不過值得一提的是，華邦電第三季獲利暴增，很大一部分來自記憶體價格上漲，而不是出貨量同步暴增。股人阿勳認為，這代表未來即使記憶體價格沒有下跌，只要漲價速度放緩，獲利成長就可能跟著降溫。「投資景氣循環股最怕什麼？不是公司開始虧錢，而是公司還在大賺特賺，股價卻已經提前反映下一輪景氣下滑。」

股人阿勳直言，比起華邦電今年能賺多少，所以他更在意的是，在目前這麼好的獲利下，明、後年還能維持多少？「派對不一定結束，但當所有人都覺得酒喝不完的時候，反而要開始注意誰準備買單了！」

此外，大摩在最新的研究報告中指出，華邦電毛利率來到70.6%，大幅高於大摩預估12.5個百分點；管理層預計第4季將持續成長，但隨著非AI需求趨緩，成長力道也有所收斂。

產能規劃部分，大摩預期高雄廠Module A 2026年底前達到每月2.4 萬至2.5萬片、16nm製程將從約2000片擴至1.6萬片，足以支撐2027年下半年的出貨需求，因此將華邦電的目標價調升至288元，並給予「優於大盤」的評等。

news.Title: 5 tech stock stalwarts have tumbled over 50%
news.Content: The technology boom version 2.0 has been driven by insatiable spending on data center infrastructure. That spending continues, but many of the companies providing the hardware necessary to run AI chatbots, like ChatGPT and Gemini, are in the midst of a brutal sell-off that's knocked the technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 down nearly 10% and flirting with correction territory. The pain has been particularly hard felt among semiconductors and cloud plays, many of which have been taken to the proverbial woodshed, including these five, which tumbled over 50% from summertime highs to recent lows: Intel: -58% Arm Holdings: -55% Oracle: -52% Sandisk: -53% KLA Corporation: -52% Source: Yahoo! Historical Quotes AI spending boom fears take root Stocks tend to move based on emotion, and now, into its fourth year, the AI trade has gotten pretty crowded. I've seen this movie before during my 30-year career, so it's not surprising to me to see the drawdowns. The usual progression: A new idea lands with many doubters and few believers. As stocks run, more converts jump on board until most of the money on the sidelines has joined the party, leaving few new buyers to step in to support stocks on pullbacks. Tech stocks like Intel didn't drop because their businesses have suddenly imploded. Instead, they've dropped because supply from sellers locking in gains has dwarfed demand. Basic economics sounds simplistic, but sometimes the simple answer is the correct one. If there's a specific catalyst beyond protecting gains, ratcheting back peak data-center spending is the most compelling. There's mounting fear that we're about to hit peak capex for data center spending in 2027, setting the stage for a slowdown. The stakes are high, given the dollars at stake. In mid-October, JPMorgan said 2026 AI capex for the five biggest hyperscalers (Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle, and Microsoft) would be $900 billion, climbing above $1 trillion in 2027. More Tech: Meta and Microsoft just sent employees a memo about Anthropic Microsoft cutting off popular software with no extension Oct. 13 Apple's biggest AI advantage may face new privacy challenge Most of that spending to date has been financed by free cash flow (and, arguably, by circular financing deals, thanks to investments from the likes of Nvidia). However, companies are increasingly turning to debt, exposing balance sheets to risk. For instance, Goldman Sachs pegged the percentage of AI capex financed by debt at 33% in 2026, up from 26% in 2025. In 2027, Goldman Sachs says 35% will be paid for by debt, totaling roughly $400 billion. Story Continues If revenue growth underdelivers or lenders get antsy and borrowing gets pricier, we could end up with a major capex reset that unravels the AI trade, or so the bear argument goes. Bank of America says demand justifies spending There's a silver lining to more judicious AI capex, though, suggests Bank of America. Analyst Vivek Arya thinks that if capex budget cuts happen, it would "lower peak profit but preserve compute scarcity, extend the AI cycle and support higher multiples over time." Think a shorter peak and a flatter runway for the entire AI cycle, which could mean less boom-and-bust action for underlying stocks. Arya thinks there's plenty of incentive to continue investing in AI, given surging backlogs. "With $2.5tn+ backlog and surging enterprise adoption, demand looks durable: scarce compute, not excess capacity, is the risk," wrote Arya in a research note shared with me. Also read : Elon Musk sends incredible news to Micron stock investors "Slower supply growth against resilient demand could lift utilization, support pricing and reduce overbuild risk. The result could be lower peak earnings, but a longer earnings runway and potentially higher multiples for chipmakers already valued as if the cycle is ending," added Arya. Major hyperscaler revenue certainly seems to support the argument for spending. Amazon's AWS revenue rose 39%, Microsoft Azure sales grew 49%, and Google AI revenue increased over 100% year over year in the third quarter, according to Arya. Are beat-down tech stocks bargain bin buys? The risk of a slowdown or debt reckoning is reflected in the most punished technology stocks. Intel has been late to the party in terms of AI-optimized chips, but optimism over U.S. fab capacity builds, and deeper pockets from U.S. and Nvidia investments caused its shares to soar before the recent drop, despite operational headwinds. At Oracle, the fear of overspending to become one of the biggest hyperscalers has raised major debt concerns, contributing to its recent drop, despite the company's argument that its backlog is solid and justifies the push. ARM Holdings makes its money by selling semiconductor designs, and a slowdown in data center spending would crimp its upside. It has historically traded at a premium valuation because of its 'asset-light/no-fab' status, making it more susceptible to drawdowns as investors press sell on so-called expensive players first. A downthrottling in capex would also be bad news for KLA Corporation, which makes inspection and measurement machines used to create semiconductors. If the data center buildout slows, so would chip demand, and the need for new fab equipment. Like ARM, KLA has long been considered a premium play in the semiconductor equipment space, trading at a higher valuation than peers such as Applied Materials and Lam Research, making it susceptible to sell-offs. SanDisk sits in a different space, given that it makes memory, but lower spending on high-end server capacity means less memory is needed. Given the 303% surge in NAND flash memory this past year, and the historical cyclical nature of memory market demand, a bit of investors' caution is warranted. It's hard to judge whether any of these individual stock drawdowns have run their course and are ready to reverse, but Arya thinks semiconductor plays aren't overpriced relative to history. "Since CY19, the SOX index has traded at 12.5x-30x forward PE multiple, ranging from a 20% discount to a 40% premium versus SPX. Today, 16.4x represents a 10% discount, consistent with AI-cycle troughs in CY23-1H26 and only 10pts above the deepest relative discount since CY19." Of course, stocks can always get cheaper, but Arya's math shows that these stocks aren't historically priced excessively, and that should give some modicum of comfort to bargain hunters, especially if Arya is right that a capex reset wouldn't trigger demand destruction nearly to the extent some fear. "The market therefore appears to be discounting capex risk before the demand data have cracked. If paying AI demand stays resilient, lower capex could reduce overbuild, preserve scarcity, extend the EPS cycle and justify higher multiples, in our opinion," concluded Arya. news.Title: What Skyworks Solutions (SWKS) Said on Its Q4 Earnings Call
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Skyworks Solutions, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Skyworks closed its Qorvo acquisition after its fiscal Q4 ended, so reported quarterly results cover legacy Skyworks only; its December-quarter outlook is for the combined company. Q4 revenue was $1.046 billion and non-GAAP EPS was $1.28, both slightly above guidance midpoints.

The combined company expects December-quarter revenue of $1.8 billion to $1.9 billion and non-GAAP EPS of $1.25 at the midpoint. Smartphone revenue is expected to decline sequentially, while Diversified Growth Markets—including data center, defense and automotive—are expected to grow.

Skyworks reiterated a target of at least $500 million in annual cost synergies from the deal, with most earnings benefits expected in the second half of fiscal 2027. Longer-term targets include mid- to high-single-digit revenue growth and 50% to 55% gross margins within 24 to 36 months.

Apple Cut iPhone 18 Orders; What Does It Mean For Suppliers?

Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS) reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results as a standalone company and outlined its first outlook as a combined business following the October 5 closing of its acquisition of Qorvo.

Chief Executive Officer and President Phil Brace said the combination brings greater scale, a broader technology portfolio and an expanded manufacturing footprint. The company will report its operations going forward in two categories: smartphone and Diversified Growth Markets.

→ LyondellBasell's Dividend Looks Safer, But a New Risk Could Change That

MarketBeat Week in Review – 06/23 - 6/27

Because the Qorvo transaction closed after Skyworks' fiscal fourth-quarter end, Skyworks' September-quarter results reflect only the legacy Skyworks business, while December-quarter guidance is on a combined-company basis.

Fourth-Quarter Results and Market Trends

For the fiscal quarter ended October 2, Skyworks reported revenue of $1.046 billion, above the midpoint of its guidance range of $1.035 billion. Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share were $1.28, $0.01 above the midpoint of guidance.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Skyworks Stock Down 16% in 2025, Poised for AI Edge Surge

Gross profit was $465 million, representing a gross margin of 44.4%, while operating expenses totaled $237 million. Operating income was $227 million, or 21.7% of revenue. Net income was $193 million. Skyworks ended the quarter with approximately $2.6 billion in cash and investments and roughly $2.5 billion in debt, including acquisition financing completed ahead of the Qorvo closing.

Story Continues

The company repurchased $107 million of stock during the quarter at an average price of $66.27 per share.

→ Exxon's Refining Profits Soared—Did Chevron Get the Same Windfall?

Mobile represented about 60% of Skyworks' standalone quarterly revenue, supported by demand from its largest customer during the company's seasonally strongest period. Brace said this was partly offset by continued weakness in Android, where Skyworks is concentrating on the premium tier.

Broad markets represented approximately 40% of revenue and grew 9% year over year in the quarter and about 10% for fiscal 2026. The company cited data center, Wi-Fi and automotive as growth drivers, while consumer IoT remained soft. Skyworks' largest customer accounted for approximately 62% of quarterly revenue, including non-smartphone products.

Brace said demand and book-to-bill trends were healthy across end markets, while timing and power products continued to gain design engagement in AI data centers. He also said automotive and industrial design activity was robust. However, management said higher input costs remain a margin headwind and are expected to persist. The company is responding through factory-load optimization, long-term supply agreements and price increases where appropriate.

Combined Business Structure and Growth Markets

On a pro forma combined basis, Skyworks said fiscal 2026 smartphone revenue was approximately $4.6 billion, down about 11% from the prior year. Management attributed the decline to expected Android weakness and content dynamics at its largest customer.

Brace said the combined company now offers a full RF front-end platform for next-generation smartphones and intends to focus investments on premium devices, where RF content is higher. He said 5G Advanced and 6G could add RF complexity through additional transmit and receive paths, spectrum bands, satellite connectivity, filters, amplifiers and antenna solutions.

Management expects the broader product portfolio to reduce reliance on individual sockets and help create steadier smartphone results. Brace characterized smartphone as a long-term low-single-digit growth business, with premium-device growth and RF content gains offset by normal integration and price compression.

Diversified Growth Markets generated about $2.9 billion in pro forma fiscal 2026 revenue, up approximately 12% year over year, according to the company. The category includes legacy Skyworks broad markets and Qorvo's High Performance Analog and Connectivity and Sensors Group.

Physical AI and connected edge: More than $1.6 billion in fiscal 2026 revenue, including Wi-Fi access points, gateways, IoT devices, industrial automation and robotics.

Defense and aerospace: Approximately $500 million, supported by modernization, space, electronic warfare and satellite constellations.

Data center and networking infrastructure: Approximately $400 million and identified by management as the company's fastest-growing market.

Automotive: Approximately $340 million, benefiting from electrification, connectivity, autonomy and infotainment trends.

Brace said demand in many of these markets exceeds the company's current ability to supply products. During the September quarter, Skyworks secured additional supply and grew its data center business by about 90% year over year, he said.

December Outlook and Integration Plan

For the December quarter, Skyworks expects combined revenue of $1.8 billion to $1.9 billion, with a midpoint of $1.85 billion. The outlook includes approximately $1.07 billion from legacy Skyworks and approximately $780 million from legacy Qorvo. The company said this will be the last quarter it provides a legacy-company revenue split.

Combined September-quarter revenue was approximately $1.98 billion, including an extra week in Qorvo's quarter that contributed about $70 million. At the December outlook midpoint, revenue would decline roughly 7% sequentially, or about 3% excluding the extra week.

Skyworks expects smartphone revenue to decline by a low-teens percentage sequentially, reflecting seasonality, Android softness and the prior quarter's extra week at Qorvo. Diversified Growth Markets revenue is expected to increase by a low-single-digit percentage sequentially despite the extra week, led by data center and defense. The category is expected to represent more than 40% of sales.

The company forecast non-GAAP gross margin of 46% to 48%, non-GAAP operating expenses of $465 million to $505 million, and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $1.25 at the revenue midpoint. It expects approximately $50 million of other expense, mainly from a full quarter of interest expense on acquisition financing.

Synergies and Long-Term Targets

Skyworks reiterated its expectation for at least $500 million in annual cost synergies from the Qorvo combination. Roughly two-thirds are expected to come from operating expenses and one-third from cost of goods sold.

Management expects approximately $150 million of operating-expense synergies in fiscal 2027 and an annualized exit run rate of approximately $250 million to $300 million. The majority of earnings benefits are expected in the second half of fiscal 2027. Brace said operating-expense savings should arrive first, while factory consolidation and other manufacturing actions will cause cost-of-goods benefits to build later.

Over the long term, Skyworks is targeting mid- to high-single-digit revenue growth. Within 24 to 36 months of closing the transaction, the company is targeting non-GAAP gross margin of 50% to 55%, non-GAAP operating margin of 30% to 35%, and adjusted EBITDA margin of 35% to 40%.

Chief Financial Officer Philip Carter said the company maintains a bias toward share repurchases while also seeking flexibility to build its cash balance following the acquisition financing. He said Skyworks would remain disciplined on accretive acquisitions that could improve gross margins and diversify its revenue base.

About Skyworks Solutions (NASDAQ:SWKS)

Skyworks Solutions, Inc (NASDAQ: SWKS) is a semiconductor company that designs and manufactures high-performance analog and mixed-signal products for wireless connectivity applications. Its portfolio includes radio-frequency front-end modules, amplifiers, filters, switches, antenna tuners, and other integrated solutions used to transmit, receive, and manage wireless signals.

The company serves a range of markets, including smartphones and other mobile devices, automotive systems, industrial equipment, home automation, medical devices, aerospace, and defense.

news.Title: 華邦電法說會行情失靈！盤中挫逾3％刷5個月最低 3萬多人「帳面1張蒸發9萬元」
news.Content:
記憶體大廠華邦電（2344）昨日舉行法說會，公布第3季稅後純益達354億元、年增逾12倍，單季EPS高達 7.58元，大賺超過半個股本，符合市場預期。但受「利多出盡」與第4季展望趨緩影響，今（4）日股價短暫上演慶祝行情後，由紅翻黑，最低觸及140.5％元，寫下5月28日以來、逾5個月盤中最低價，和 6月22日高點233.5元相比，短短5個月內下跌近4成，3萬多人追在高點，帳上一張已蒸發9.15萬元。分析師表示，短線主要受到PC消費需求放緩及明年記憶體漲幅收斂影響，使市場趨於觀望，不過，目前記憶體三雄本益比不到5倍、評價極度便宜，投資人可把握拉回時機逢低布局。

華邦電今天盤中向上衝高至148元即遭拋壓翻黑，最低下探140.5元，跌3.8％，股價寫下5個月盤中最低價。

回顧華邦電今年6月22日盤中最高233.5元，當周受益人數46萬3,762人，和前一周的42萬7,925人相比，增加3萬5837人，假設這3萬多人都追在高點，如今隨著華邦電失守200元關卡，又創5個月最低，帳上已蒸發9.15萬元。

針對華邦電「強勁財報難擋股價拉回」的現象，國泰證期顧問處協理郭經緯分析，主要受限於兩大隱憂：

第一，第4季營運動能趨緩

華邦電總經理陳沛銘於法說會中坦言，儘管AI需求旺盛，但受到PC等消費性電子需求放緩影響，第4季公司營運成長動能將相對平緩。

第二， 記憶體報價漲幅面臨收斂

陳沛銘雖指出明年記憶體市場依然供不應求，但調研機構與法人預估，包括NAND Flash與 DRAM（DDR）明年全年的價格漲幅，將從今年的倍數暴漲收斂至20%至30%左右。在報價漲幅趨緩下，短線股價難免受壓。

南亞科營收連 12 個月創新高也不漲

此外，DRAM 大廠南亞科（2408）昨日才公告 10 月合併營收達464.76億元，年增 487.73%），已連續12個月改寫單月歷史新高，且總經理李培瑛日前於法說會強調，第 4 季DRAM平均銷售單價（ASP）與毛利率將持續上漲，AI帶動的供需缺口非常大。但今日南亞科股價同樣不改頹勢，盤中最低觸及400.5元、重挫2.55%。

旺宏（2337）盤中雖一度大漲3.4%衝上91.3元，隨後也由紅翻黑下探87.6元，9字頭大關得而復失。

郭經緯指出，旺宏主攻利基型記憶體，南亞科則集中於DDR4與DDR5產品。儘管短線市場因報價漲幅收斂而進入觀望，但從估值角度來看，目前記憶體三雄的股價均處於歷史低檔，以明年預估獲利計算，本益比甚至不到 5 倍，「股價整體評價相當便宜」。

郭經緯進一步補充，雖然記憶體價格暴漲期過去，使族群股價短線轉為「區間操作」，但華邦電與南亞科題材後勁仍強，最大的潛在利多在於「高殖利率」。

由於兩家公司今年獲利均出現爆發性成長，若以過去的現金股利發放率推算，華邦電與南亞科明年的現金股息殖利率均有機會突破 10%。預計到了明年上半年，將展現強大的配息吸引力，進一步吸引高股息 ETF 與被動型資金進駐卡位。因此，在企業獲利持續向上、本益比偏低且有超高殖利率護體下，建議長線投資人無須過度悲觀，可把握股價拉回時機逢低分批布局。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: 《DJ在線》客戶搶簽長約，台記憶體三廠態度不同
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-04 09:02:17 周佩宇 發佈

記憶體客戶爭取供貨保障，長期供貨協議（LTA）也從採購安排，延伸成原廠擴產與投資的重要依據，不過南亞科（2408）、華邦電（2344）及旺宏（2337）的做法並不一致，但都強調，長約是否能連結客戶需求、設備投資與產品路線，比單純追求合約年限更重要。南亞科已有五至七成長約覆蓋，華邦正為新廠洽談搭配預付款的策略合作，旺宏目前則仍未簽訂LTA。

南亞科的長約已進入實際履約與續約階段。公司目前LTA覆蓋率約50%至70%，期間從一季至三年，客戶積極爭取延長供應期限。第三季售價大幅上升，也反映部分過去低價議定的舊約完成交貨後，開始適用新的合約價格，顯示長約雖能增加供需能見度，議價時點與續約安排仍會影響獲利反映速度。

後續擴建則以有客戶長約支持的AI專案為主要目標，林口5A廠預計明(2027)年第一季裝機，2028年底月投片目標3萬片、2030年底達5萬片；設備交期延長、安裝與驗證均需時間，現階段取得的長期需求，將分階段轉成未來供給。

華邦電則將長約與新廠設備投資直接連結。公司表示，希望選擇數家產品路線相符的策略夥伴，涵蓋2029年Module B新產能開出後至2032年的需求，目前有意洽談者已超過10家。合作模式包含客戶先支付訂金或預付款，支應設備投資，再由未來產品供應回饋，各家條件分別協商；例如車用客戶由LPDDR4轉向LPDDR5，若與華邦電未來路線一致，就更有建立長期合作的基礎。供給端則採分階段建置，這次核准731億元資本支出，涵蓋土建、機電及長交期設備，尚未包含全部設備支出，Module B月產6萬片也不會一次到位。這種安排將客戶未來用量、產品轉換與擴產節奏一起考量，也讓華邦電能提前處理設備採購及資金需求。

旺宏則保留不同選擇，董事長吳敏求提到，雖有許多客戶上門洽談，然仍未與任何一家簽訂LTA，因不把長約本身視為保障，更重視每份合約是否公平、互利，並持續優先服務長期合作客戶。而旺宏的擴產瓶頸仍在設備交期，他透露將拜訪設備商催交貨，而增加供給也不排除透過購併或與其他廠商合作。目前擴產規畫首階段新增產能會在2027年下半年量產，後續158億元投資的設備、預計2027年下半年至年底到位，量產落在2028年。

旺宏擴產評估購併、合作，接班人選已定

news.Title: 《DJ在線》AI排擠效應，台廠攻記憶體缺口策略分化
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-04 09:02:13 周佩宇 發佈

記憶體供給吃緊，台灣三家原廠的投資與產品取捨也逐漸拉開差異。從最新今(2026)年第三季法說會及會後採訪來看，南亞科（2408）維持跨世代DRAM供應，保留DDR4轉向DDR5的彈性；華邦電（2344）以DDR4、LPDDR4為近期主力，下一步低功耗產品瞄準LPDDR5；旺宏（2337）則將新增產能集中於NAND與eMMC，NOR則轉向高容量及高可靠度應用。三原廠共同面對大廠產品升級留下的供給缺口，但資源投入並未走向同一條路。

南亞科的策略是兼顧既有客戶與新世代產品。公司第三季DDR4與LPDDR4合計占產品營收逾六成，DDR5約一成；雖有能力依需求將DDR5比重提高至四成，惟目前DDR4客戶需求仍強，尚無大幅調整必要。公司也指出，DDR4、LPDDR4整體市場雖逐步縮小，剩餘需求相對仍大，依然具有經營空間，且應用從PC、車用及工業，延伸至伺服器、網通、儲存與系統管理。公司也同步拓展客製化AI記憶體，目前AI基礎設施相關營收已超過兩成，後續成長方向是增加高容量、高頻寬及客製化產品，但也不會棄守仍缺貨的成熟世代。

華邦電則更強調產品與客戶長期路線的契合。公司表示，現階段DDR4缺口已相當可觀，因此不必積極搶進標準型DDR5，後續低功耗產品規劃由LPDDR4走向LPDDR5，尤其重視車用等生命週期較長的需求。車用、工業客戶採用特定記憶體後，轉換不易，長期供貨能力因而成為爭取合作的重要條件；伺服器與基礎架構客戶也是新增需求來源。支撐這條路線的是20奈米DDR4、LPDDR4，以及已開始放量、預期明年顯著增加營收貢獻的16奈米製程。Flash方面，華邦持續提高高容量NOR與24奈米產品貢獻，AI需求除伺服器運算，也涵蓋交換器及SmartNIC等網通設備。

旺宏相對加重NAND的重要性，尤其是eMMC。公司第三季NAND相關業務含eMMC占營收47%，略高於NOR的46%，其中eMMC營收季增27%。董事長吳敏求說明，大廠淡出部分低容量NAND帶來承接機會，然既有產能卻有限，因此新增產能將投入NAND、eMMC，部分原供NOR使用的產能也轉往NAND；明年eMMC以96層3D NAND為主力，藉製程集中與較佳獲利能力提高資源效率。市場選擇上，目前NAND含eMMC仍以通訊應用為大宗，第三季占比52%，工業、車用等長期需求亦持續布局；NOR則保留資料中心、太空通訊、醫療及車用等市場，高容量產品仍持續開發。

由此可見，三家產品分化的重點，在於選擇哪些缺口值得持續投資、哪些客戶值得保留產能；南亞科與華邦在DDR4、LPDDR4仍有重疊，華邦與旺宏也同樣經營NOR，但各自優先投入的製程、產品與新增產能已有差異。

news.Title: 智原推強化版乙太網路PHY IP，攻AI智慧製造等應用
news.Content:
MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-04 09:01:31 新聞中心 發佈

智原(3035)昨(3)日發表支援EtherCAT的強化版10/100乙太網路PHY IP解決方案於聯電(2303)製程，滿足AI智慧製造、工業自動化與人形機器人對即時通訊及同步運動控制日益增長的需求。公司指出，此預先驗證IP支援少於100微秒的EtherCAT傳輸時間，並透過EtherCAT分散式時鐘(Distributed Clocks, DC)實現少於0.1微秒的同步精度，同時通過嚴謹的ETG.7000合規性及IEC 61000-4測試，協助客戶簡化ASIC開發並提升產品開發效率。

此智原Ethernet PHY IP採用DSP架構，結合穩健的類比電路設計，提供優異的抗雜訊能力，並能在嚴峻的電氣干擾環境下維持穩定運作。該PHY IP已依據ETG.7000合規性測試規範通過EtherCAT裝置相容性及網路互通性測試，以及涵蓋靜電放電(ESD)、輻射射頻(RF)、電氣快速瞬變/脈衝群(EFT/Burst) 、突波(Surge)及傳導射頻(Conducted RF)等干擾的關鍵IEC 61000-4電磁相容性(EMC)測試。其可靠度亦透過長達一小時以上的電快速瞬變脈衝群抗擾度測試進一步驗證，在電磁閥產生高頻EFT/Burst脈衝的條件下，確認硬體保護機制及通訊完整性。透過IP層級的強化設計完成預先驗證，可協助客戶減少系統層級的設計與驗證工作，並降低開發風險。

智原營運長林世欽表示：「即時連線能力與優異的抗雜訊穩健性，對次世代工業系統至關重要，尤其在AI日益融入製造與實體機器的趨勢下更是如此。智原將EtherCAT相容性與EMC驗證整合於IP層級，協助客戶簡化系統開發，並降低高額的重新驗證風險。未來智原將持續擴展乙太網路IP產品布局，支援工業AI、軟體定義汽車及人形機器人等應用，包括10/100/1000BASE-T1及單對乙太網路(Single Pair Ethernet, SPE)解決方案。」
