news.Title: Tower Semiconductor (TSEM) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.Content:
Image source: The Motley Fool.

DATE

Monday, Nov. 2, 2026

CALL PARTICIPANTS

Chief People, Communications and Investor Relations Officer - Noit Levy

Chief Executive Officer - Russell Ellwanger

President - Marco Racanelli

Chief Financial Officer - Oren Shirazi

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email pr@fool.com

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator: Good day, and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the Tower Semiconductor Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call. [Operator Instructions] Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to hand the conference over to your first speaker today, Noit Levy, Chief People, Communications and Investor Relations Officer. Please go ahead.

Noit Levi-Karoubi: Hello and thank you for joining us. Welcome to Tower Semiconductor's Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results Conference Call. With us today are Mr. Russell Ellwanger, Chief Executive Officer; Dr. Marco Racanelli, President; and Mr. Oren Shirazi, Chief Financial Officer. Before we begin, please note that certain statements made during today's call may be forward-looking and subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. These risks are detailed in our SEC filings, Form 20-F and 6-K as well as filings with the Israeli Securities Authority, all available on our website. Tower assumes no obligation to update forward-looking statements. Our third quarter 2026 results are prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP.

Some data presented may include non-GAAP financial measures as defined under SEC Regulation G. Reconciliation to GAAP figures and full explanations are provided in today's press release and financial tables. For your reference, a supporting slide deck is available on our website and integrated into this webcast. With that, I'll turn the call over to our CEO, Mr. Russell Ellwanger. Russell?

Russell Ellwanger: Thank you, Levy. Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining our call. We have much to discuss. We will speak not only to the strength of our current performance, but very importantly, on what comes next, namely the great business and financial strength with which we will be opening 2027, the visibility we have into the future demand, the realization of investments to fully capture that demand, 2028, 2029 further customer commitments, and our significant growth in customer-aligned value creation activities for 2029 and beyond. Indeed, a long-term value creation campaign with boots on the ground, providing real-time measurable financial and strategic achievements.

Story Continues

During the third quarter, we continued to deliver record results while building upon our technology leadership and expanding capacity with increasing customer commitments to support a significantly higher level of revenue and earnings in the quarters and years ahead. At the center of this growth are our silicon photonics platforms, where accelerating AI infrastructure demand, expanding customer programs and long-term capacity commitments continue to increase Tower's scale and strategic position. This momentum is complemented by strong execution across our broader portfolio of differentiated analog semiconductor technologies. We are entering the strongest growth phase in our history.

Our third quarter performance demonstrates that the strategic decisions we have made are translating into record revenue, expanding earnings power and significant visibility into the years ahead. Third quarter revenue was $526 million as compared to $396 million in the third quarter of 2025, a 33% year-over-year growth, resulting in a net profit of $120 million or 23% net margin, up from 14% net margin a year ago. Our fourth quarter 2026 mid-range revenue guidance is $600 million, which achievement would result in a 2026 full year revenue of $2 billion against a full year 2025 revenue of $1.57 billion.

Achieving a $2.4 billion revenue run rate is most significant as our demand and start plans do not indicate the typical industry first quarter seasonality. To the contrary, we expect to see continued growth. Hence, the starting point of 2027 is targeted to be higher than the $2.4 billion annual begin run rate and greater than 45% increase as compared to the first quarter of 2026 revenue starting point. Later in the call, we will share details that underscore the strong quarter-over-quarter growth we are driving in 2027. Moving into our businesses. Please refer to Slide 4 as reference for the Q3 revenue breakdown by technology.

The third quarter was another quarter of strong operational execution by our teams, both in the expansion and repurposing of 4 of our 5 factories towards substantially higher infrastructure mix with a background of growth activities in all of our core businesses. Our silicon photonics business is experiencing exceptional growth. To support accelerating customer demand, we are expanding capacity across 4 manufacturing sites, a business that contributed approximately $240 million of silicon photonics revenue in Q3 2026 alone. With substantial capacity coming online this quarter, we expect year-end capacity to be approximately double the level that supported the Q3 2026 silicon photonics revenue.

This positions us for significant revenue ramp in the first and second quarters of 2027 as the new start rates move through the fab and ship, establishing a new substantially higher sustainable baseline for the quarters ahead. and thereby also achieving a full ROI within 1 year for the previously announced $920 million CapEx investments. Additionally, the execution of our released Track-1 300-millimeter expansion is progressing ahead of schedule with all tools ordered and slotted with full production starts targeted for Q3 2027. Including the Track-1 300-millimeter expansion, our silicon photonics start capacity is targeted to increase by 3x versus the level that supported the Q3 2026 $250 million SiPho -- $240 million SiPho shipments.

Importantly, this capacity is spoken for. Through a combination of signed agreements and contracts in advanced stages of negotiation, we have secured customer demand commitments for both 200-millimeter and 300-millimeter production and now having extended it to include 2029, at which time our incremental Track-2 plant capacity ramp is well underway, ultimately quadrupling our 300-millimeter Japan capacity. Of note, all expansion is planned to continue to be self-funded. In addition to serving the rapidly growing market, largely of pluggable scale-out transceivers, we continue many activities with Tier 1 customers that take advantage of new opportunities expanding our served market.

The most significant of these is the change in form factor towards near package optics or NPO that promises to add scale-up opportunities to our clearly established leading position in the scale-out market. In the view of most analysts, NPO scale-out can double the optical transceiver market. To this end, we are prototyping NPO products with more than 10 of our top customers. NPO can more often integrate transmit and receive functions in our SiPho die, expanding our silicon SAM versus the traditional pluggable market, where normally only transmit function is built into the SiPho die.

NPO can also improve our position in the electrical IC SiGe market as most implementations of NPO will replace the DSP to improve cost, power and latency with SiGe TIAs and drivers and at that with greater footprint due to the increased incorporation of equalizer functionality, expanding our SiGe market opportunity. To this end, we have announced this quarter a substantial capacity agreement with Semtech and are seeing further unprecedented growth opportunities for our SiGe business. Longer term, we are building the capability to integrate new material into our SiPho platform to further expand our served available market.

In one such example, we announced initial production for new photonics with a new technology where we integrated indium phosphide lasers within our silicon photonics die. This is done through a die-to-wafer attach of indium phosphide InP chiplets further processed in our factory to create a final die that incorporates indium phosphide lasers within our silicon photonics. As this technology ramps, we gain access to the laser market and additional multiples of increase in serviceable market. This die-to-wafer technology is now being deployed with other materials such as thin-film lithium niobate to provide 400 gigabit per lane next-generation differentiated products to our Tier 1 lead customers.

Beyond the optical transceiver market, our SiPho platform, combined with heterogeneous integration capability has emerged as a go-to solution for silicon photonics-based optical circuit switches. Silicon photonics-based solid-state OCS are emerging as a strong contender against MEMS or other niche solutions because of fast nanosecond level switching speeds, the CMOS manufacturing scale and compatibility with the CPO/NPO ecosystem for tighter system integration. Finally, we have been a significant player in coherent SiPho products for Marvell used in data center connect applications, as we have discussed in the past.

This technology is now being evaluated for inside data center scale across applications, which could as well significantly expand the sector of the SiPho market, we already have strong position and differentiated technology. Longer term, we are also investing in several scale-up and scale-in wide and slow technologies, which promise high total bandwidth by creating large parallel links at lower speed through the use of micro LEDs and/or VCSELs. We have several active engagements ongoing with Tier 1 customers with the potential of high volume in a new facet of the optical communication market.

As stated earlier, NPO is providing an expanding market for silicon germanium TIA and drivers, resulting in unprecedented customer demand being served now from 3 200-millimeter factories and 1 300-millimeter factory. In tandem with our capacity expansion, we continue to advance our technology road map and are happy to report that our H6 next-generation silicon germanium technology is seeing strong design-in momentum already in production for the most demanding products. The strength of our technology was also reflected recently when Semtech, a strategic silicon germanium partner of more than 2 decades, received an innovation award at ECOC '26 for its Optical Interconnect Solutions. Our 300-millimeter capacity corridor in Agrate, Italy delivered its highest RFSOI revenue quarter-to-date.

We also set new records for the number of product tape-outs for Fab 10, demonstrating the strength of our long-standing customer relationships and the exceptional execution by our Fab 10 team to deliver the technology road map, extending the design win momentum on our industry-leading 300-millimeter RFSOI platforms. We expect this trajectory to continue over the coming quarters. Demand for Tower's BCD technologies continues to strengthen across both 200-millimeter and 300-millimeter platforms with about 10% year-over-year growth. This growth is driven not only by the rapid expansion of AI and cloud data centers, but also by growing customer success in mobile and automotive applications.

This momentum is reflected in increasing customer commitments with several strategic accounts entering into long-term agreements at higher ASPs, resulting in forecasted 20% higher blended prices for 2027 versus 2026. In CIS and displays, we have started production of a new high-speed global shutter sensor for high-end video cameras with one of the DSLR MILC industry leaders. Together with our lead customers, we are driving next phase of business growth, building demand toward the significant additional capacity that will come online with the Uozu expansion. We're also working closely with our OLED on silicon display customers to provide capacity for their expected steep ramp in 2027. Looking at utilization.

During the third quarter, all of our 200-millimeter fabs operated at utilization levels of 85% to 90%. Our 300-millimeter 12-inch fab continues to be fully utilized, well above our 85% utilization model. And as stated, substantial capacity is being added to all sites in accordance with extreme growing demand. To summarize, we entered the second half of 2026 with strong business momentum, supported by broad customer demand across our differentiated technology platforms and continued high utilization across our entire manufacturing footprint. Importantly, the strength we see extends beyond the current quarter, well beyond.

Customer engagements, design activity and demand visibility continue to reinforce our confidence in growth opportunities ahead, enabled by the unique significant value, which each of our specialized analog technologies provide. Our prospects are very good and even getting better with all of our key business units experiencing increased demand with expected revenue growth throughout 2027. SiPho and silicon germanium are experiencing unprecedented growth, having achieved majority share of pluggable scale-out market. We're not only enjoying the substantial market growth of this segment, but by having close partnerships and cooperations with the market leaders, we are enjoying rich developments, increasing our served market, targeting to continue proliferation of our differentiated technologies into multifaceted applications.

The number of advanced NPO engagements is just one of the many indicators of rich partnerships capturing the future. As a summary point, our Q4 '26 SiPho annualized run rate is expected to exceed $1.1 billion with significant target further increases in Q1 '27. We will end this year in an extremely exciting position. With that, I'd like to turn the call to our CFO, Mr. Oren Shirazi. Oren, please?

Oren Shirazi: Thank you, Russell. Hello, everyone. The third quarter marked another significant step-up in Tower's financial performance with record revenue, record gross profit and strong operating leverage across the P&L. Revenue increased [ 36% ] year-over-year to $526 million, while gross profit increased by 92%. Operating profit increased by 2.5x and net profit reached $120 million, representing 23% net margin or 2.2x as compared to the third quarter of 2025. These results demonstrate our accelerating growth is translating into substantial earnings expansion. They also reflect the increasing contribution of our differentiated higher-value technologies and the strength of our operating model as we scale.

Importantly, we are entering this next phase of growth from a position of financial strength, evidenced by our strong balance sheet and cash position. With customer long-term contracts that secure our CapEx investments will yield quick ROIs by providing increased visibility into our customers' future demand and high capacity utilization. I will now review the quarterly financial performance, followed by our balance sheet, cash flow and capital investment plan and conclude with the financial framework underlying our long-term business model. Looking into the P&L.

Revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $526 million, a record in the company's history, representing 14% quarter-over-quarter growth as compared to $460 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $130 million higher year-over-year or 36% year-over-year growth. Gross profit for the third quarter of 2026 was a record $179 million, an increase of 92% compared to $93 million in the third quarter of 2025. Operating profit for the third quarter of 2026 was $127 million, 2.5x the operating profit in the third quarter of 2025. Net profit for the third quarter of 2026 was $120 million, reflecting 23% net margin. Net profit is more than double the $54 million in the third quarter of 2025.

Earnings per share for the third quarter of 2026 were $1.06 basic and $1.05 diluted as compared to $0.48 basic and $0.47 diluted in the third quarter of 2025. Moving to our balance sheet. Prepayments received from SiPho customers mostly towards 2027 capacity reservation, including the $290 million previously announced prepayments received in the first quarter of 2026 are presented in the balance sheet as liabilities under short- and long-term customer advances and are included in the 2026 cash flow report as cash flow from operating activities. Our balance sheet continues to be very strong, evidenced by the following indicators and financial ratios.

As of the end of September 2026, our assets totaled $4 billion, primarily comprised of $1.8 billion in net fixed assets, predominantly Fab machinery and $2 billion of current assets. Shareholders' equity reached a record of $3.2 billion, representing 80% of total assets. Our current ratio is strong at about 3.7x and our increased long-term asset balance mainly reflects the Newport Fab lease prepayment as well as other prepayments. Hedging, I would like now to describe our currency hedging activities. Regarding Japanese yen, since the majority of TPSCo's revenue is denominated in yen and the vast majority of TPSCo's costs are also in yen, we have a natural hedge over most of our Japanese business and operations.

To mitigate part of the remaining yen exposure, we execute 0 cost cylinder transactions to hedge currency fluctuations. Hence, while the yen exchange rate against the dollar may fluctuate, there is a limited impact on our margins. Regarding the Israeli shekel, while we have no revenue in this currency, a portion of our cost in Israel is denominated in shekel. So we also hedge a large portion of that currency risk by entering into 0 cost cylinder transactions to mitigate the exposure. Hence, while the shekel exchange rate against the dollar may fluctuate as seen over the past few quarters, during which the shekel appreciated strongly against the dollar, the impact on our margins is limited.

Now moving to CapEx investment plan. As previously announced, in order to support the increasing SiPho and 5G demand, we are executing a $920 million investment plan to expand capacity and capability of SiGe and SiPho equipment across our 8-inch fabs in Israel, Newport Beach and Texas as well as our 12-inch Uozu fab in Japan. These investments are progressing ahead of schedule in terms of on-schedule tools, technology, process qualification, equipment arrivals and ramp plans. and are supported by customer contracts and prepayment.

Approximately 65% of this $920 million CapEx investment has been paid to date and is included in our cash flow for investing activities for the reporting period through the third quarter of 2026, while the remaining 35% is expected to be paid during Q4 '26 and H1 '27. As Russell noted earlier, we expect 1 year full ROI from this investment. In addition, we are executing on the Track-1 Japan 300-millimeter CapEx plan by issuing purchase orders for 12-inch SiPho capacity and capability tools that will significantly increase our 12-inch SiPho capacity. These CapEx payments are scheduled for 2027 and 2028. Business model.

As recently announced, the company updated its business model, which now includes the planned investment in Arai facility, formerly Fab 6, to repurpose it for 12-inch SiPho wafer manufacturing, thereby maximizing the company's 12-inch wafer output in Japan, supported by METI, Japan's Ministry of Economic, Trade and Industry. The updated model is based on forward-looking operational business and financial assumptions, including the assumption that all fabs will operate at 85% utilization post full installation and qualification of the $920 million in SiPho and 5G CapEx investments. We continue to ramp up SiPho and 5G capacity and capability in our Fabs 2, 3, 7 and 9.

And in addition, we are working to repurpose the Arai facility and qualify the new equipment tools to be installed there. Assumptions regarding forward-looking wafer selling prices for existing and future products and flow and forward-looking assumptions regarding cost and completion dates for the successful qualification of tools to be installed, process technologies to be qualified and customer products to be qualified and ordered from the company. Under this updated financial model, we assume we target $3.6 billion in annual revenue, which is $760 million higher than the February model target, reflecting 27% revenue increase. $1.63 billion annual gross profit, resulting in 45% gross margin as compared to 39% in the prior model.

This annual gross profit is $510 million higher than the previous February 2026 model, representing 67% incremental gross profit derived from the incremental $760 million revenue, reflecting our enhanced product mix. We also target $1.38 billion of annual operating profit, resulting in 38% operating margin as compared to 32% in the prior model. And we target $1.2 billion in annual net profit, resulting in a 33% net margin as compared to 26% in the prior model and 20% in the second quarter of '26 and as compared to 23% in the third quarter of '26.

This annual net profit of $1.2 billion target is $450 million higher than the pre February 2026 model, representing 59% incremental net profit derived from the incremental $760 million revenue, reflecting our enhanced product mix. That concludes my prepared remarks. Now I'd like to turn the call back to the operator so we can take your questions. Operator?

Operator: [Operator Instructions] We take our first question and it comes from the line of Cody Acree from StoneX Financial.

Cody Grant Acree: Congrats on the progress. It's great to see. Maybe, Russell, thanks for the exponential increases that you gave in capacity additions. Maybe if you can just help me to just work out the math there. Can you just level set us with the $920 million of CapEx program now firmly on track and ahead of schedule. Can you level set your fiscal '28 capacity support now for SiPho and SiGe from a revenue standpoint?

Russell Ellwanger: I would prefer not to give an exact target on revenue, but I can give you a multiplication against the previous quarter revenue as far as raw capacity. So as stated, the previous quarter, Q3 was $240 million of SiPho revenue. We will finish Q4 with 2x the start capacity that drove that revenue in Q3. So 2x the starts of the Q3 shipments. That revenue will become the run rate in Q2 when there's a full Q1 of that start rate and the December, January, February all ship within Q2. Then in Q3, we will add another 1x of that, so 3x of the Q3 shipments through the expansion that we are doing in the Fab 7 Arai factory.

That will be plus/minus the SiPho capabilities off of investments that we have already announced. We are evaluating and will most likely be announcing shortly additional SiPho announcements where we've been able to identify further areas for expansion, predominantly in 2 of our 200-millimeter sites. And we've not yet released that. We've not yet talked about the amount of CapEx nor the amount of capacity that would increase, but it's another significant tranche on top of it. But the capacity, if you go against the multiplications that I talked about, that would give somewhere of a $2.85 billion to $2.9 billion SiPho run rate as of Q3 in start rates.

However, that is really not 100% accurate because it does not include what we're doing with integrated laser. So that is outside of it and on top of it and a substantial forecast in and of itself. So if that kind of level sets the baseline of SiPho revenue for everything that has been announced and will be fully implemented on starts as of -- by plan as of the third quarter of 2027 is somewhere a bit above the $2.8 billion run rate.

Cody Grant Acree: That's very helpful, Russell. That's a great place to start for Q3. Maybe with all of that, then it sounds like your summer update for your business model, your $3.6 billion and $1.2 billion in net profit that Oren just ran through may already be too conservative. Would you agree with that?

Russell Ellwanger: No comment. No, I think it's an aggressive target. But certainly, we wouldn't be giving a target to the Street that we don't have very, very high confidence that we will meet.

Cody Grant Acree: And then lastly, if I may, for Oren, you had a very, very high incremental margin this quarter. First time we've seen it in the 60s, 62%. How sustainable do you think that level is? Is that a new baseline? Or will that fluctuate as you get new tools in and start depreciating that capacity?

Oren Shirazi: Yes, exactly like you said, this quarter, still not all the tools started their depreciation schedule from the fact that I said that 65% of the tools were paid, so you can maybe understand that approximately 65% of those $920 million tools started depreciation and the other not, and there is the second tranche of Track-1. So we will experience additional depreciation coming in later. And this is why the long-term model, I don't think has the 65% incremental gross margin that we saw this quarter and has like 55%, 58% usually. And so we repeat our same forecast of 55% to 58% incremental gross profit.

Operator: Now we take our next question and the question comes from the line of Vijay Rakesh from Mizuho.

Vijay Rakesh: Russell and Oren, just a question on the SiPho side. Obviously, you're doing multiple versions of NPO. You have external laser internal integrated lasers. Can you talk to how you're seeing the pricing and contracts line up as you look at some of the newer layouts and NPO going out? And a quick follow-up.

Russell Ellwanger: It's a very, very interesting question and a good question. Our long-term contracts include pricing targets. There's been maybe some inputs from time to time that curtails price increases, but it does the opposite. As new players possibly come into the game, one way that they try to get into market is by deeply discounting. Now those that deeply discount typically do it because they don't compete technically. But what our contracts do is that they set a bar of a starting position, not that if market really would demand some lowering of prices that we wouldn't adhere to being reasonable with our customers.

But our pricing is set very, very well in our long-term contracts and pricing targets are within all of our contracts. NPO, I don't want to give an exact number for NPO. I don't think that, that would be a proper thing to do. But NPO certainly stays with our trend of any new platform resets a pricing curve as far as getting a higher ASP. So the way that over time, anybody protects high margins is by being the fastest to deliver products and taking advantage of being the first in the market to help a customer grow their market by being the first with their specific end application.

So I would just want to say that our pricing is solid, it's good, and it's very sustainable through the way that we have gone about our long-term agreements. NPO will have a higher starting point than a pluggable, and that makes sense as it's a more advanced technology platform. Our pluggable starting point wasn't bad and isn't bad right now, as is seen by the incremental margin drop down. If that...

Vijay Rakesh: And then on the -- yes. That's very helpful. I think one of the things that were coming up at OCP US was obviously, people are starting to talk more about 3.2T, 400 gig per lane. As you look at your NPO demand backlog, are you seeing more engagements start to dial up at 3.2 gig? Is that a higher dollar, more complicated layout on SiPho? Like how do you look at that mix and the opportunity?

Russell Ellwanger: The answer to both parts of your question is yes.

Vijay Rakesh: Is the mix higher on 3.2T?

Russell Ellwanger: Yes.

Operator: Now we're going to take our next question. And the question comes from the line of Simon Coles from Barclays.

Simon Coles: There's a lot of chatter about competition on SiPho given how well you guys are executing. You started ramping 12-inch yields, I think, late last year, early this year. Can you just give us an update on sort of that progress and how that's sort of helping you maintain your leadership?

Russell Ellwanger: I'm not sure I 100% understand your question. I'll answer what I think it is. And if you need further clarification, please ask. We indeed started shipping revenue volumes in the first quarter of 2027 at extremely high yields, really high yields. With our 300-millimeter platforms, we have very special applications. We have an amazing demux capability that I think is absolutely best in the world. So we've added multiple new types of platforms. Most of the NPO tape-outs that we're doing are being done at 300-millimeter. And those are 16 lane, 32-lane applications right now.

And the pluggable that we're doing also just has incredible performance, substantially better on insertion loss than I think anyone else can be even coming close to it. So if that answers your question, the ramp that we're doing at 300-millimeter is quite substantial. We have stated that from where we'll be at in Q1 on 300-millimeter, which on equivalent is somewhere about 10,000, 200-millimeter. By the end of the year, we'll be increasing that by the third quarter of the year, we'll be increasing that by 3x and then incrementally increasing as well in 2028 and ultimately, very, very big increase as the new shell is built at the end of 2028. Did that answer your question?

I hope it did.

Operator: And the next question comes from the line of Sahej Singh from Stifel.

Sahej Singh: Russell, your framing was very helpful. So maybe let me build on that. You said 3Q revenue -- SiPho revenue was about $240 million. That adds -- and that -- the 3Q '27 step adds another 1x on top of that capacity through Fab 7 and Arai.

Russell Ellwanger: Triples it.

Sahej Singh: Sorry.

Sahej Singh: Triples it. But I guess by my math, that would be roughly $960 million a year. So that's $200 million more than the $760 million Track 1 adds to the '28 model. So first, if I'm understanding that correctly, is that all Track-1? Or does it include remaining capacity from the $920 million program? And then second, in those same units, as Track-2 ramps towards the quadrupling of Japan's 300-millimeter, how -- roughly how many multiples does Track-2 add? Is that another 1, 2x? Or would it be more than that as a floor?

Oren Shirazi: For the first question, what Russell said is that today, including -- I mean, today, the total revenue from the shipments of Q3 reflected is $240 million and tripling it means $720 million, not $960 million. So $720 million per quarter run rate towards -- I think it was Cody's answer -- question about 2028. So Russell said Q3 '27 capacity baseline can support capacity, $720 a quarter. So times 4, it's $2.8 billion, which Russell mentioned, right, not $960 million.

Sahej Singh: Okay. That's helpful. And then on...

Russell Ellwanger: I also did say that there's additional SiPho activities that are not included in that. So I'm not saying that we are gated at the $2.8 billion. There's the integrated laser, many things that do not include into that. If we're talking specifically about the quadrupling, we're quadrupling what we're talking of the present capacity, which is somewhere about 10,000 wafer per month in our Fab 7 300-millimeter, and that will be quadrupled to 40,000 wafer per month approximately. I mean we don't know the exact numbers as of yet, the build hasn't been done.

But what that does then is an extreme increase if it was all on SiPho because you're putting 2.25 against each 300-millimeter wafer as you compare to 200-millimeter. So if you were going to 40,000 on 200-millimeter equivalents, you're close to 100,000 wafers.

Sahej Singh: That's very helpful. I guess, Russell, the P times Q sort of math, you're pointing to the 2.25x die size increase on the 300-millimeter, which makes sense. But Track-2 is also predominantly going to be NPO, which means the content uplift is also there, and that sort of changes the like-for-like math, I think that most investors are trying to do. Could you maybe give some color on that as well?

Russell Ellwanger: The price per wafer, again, had stated as we go to NPO, it resets the price target, right, to reset the pricing curve. What bigger chips do is they create more silicon demand. So the NPO will -- the more lanes that you put into it, the more silicon you're going to need to ship the same amount of chips. That physically change the cost of the silicon other than the higher the integration, the newer the technology, the higher the starting price point.

Sahej Singh: Yes, correct. I mean I'm on the same page. I think it's mostly about sort of sizing higher. But one last one for me, and it's maybe on timing. I guess you said Track-2 is well underway, and I believe that Fab 7...

Russell Ellwanger: No. I said Track-2 will be well underway in 2028.

Sahej Singh: By '29 -- '28.

Russell Ellwanger: '28, we'll start with the buildings in '29 when we have our last contracts that we are signing now. Again, we extended our capacity contract to 2029, which is a very, very good thing for us, tremendous visibility and commitment. So we had stated the 1-year ROI for the $920 million investment that we did predominantly for 200-millimeter expansion. By having customer commitments it really adds your confidence on short-term ROI. And the ROI that we're -- it's an extremely aggressive model.

Sahej Singh: The question just being Track-2, I think you take ownership of Fab 7 April 1. Could that start earlier, Meaning, I guess, simply put, could Track-2 output come in sort of second half of '28? Or is it almost all a '29 driver?

Russell Ellwanger: Could is possible. But what we're really believing is the amount of time to build, we're quite confident that the '29 will be the expansion. If it can be accelerated by a quarter, that's certainly our target, right? I mean it's any investment, the quicker that you can start shipping, the quicker you please your customers and the quicker you please your investors.

Operator: Now we take our next question and the question comes from the line of Mehdi Hosseini from Susquehanna International Group.

Unknown Analyst: This is Sebastian filling in for Mehdi. I guess piggybacking on the competitive landscape question into 2027. Given the ramp of one of your major competitors in terms of PIC capacity, how should we think about the market share in silicon photonics and silicon germanium for 2027? And I have a follow-up.

Russell Ellwanger: Let me ask Dr. Racanelli to speak to that as he's directly interacting with driving the BUs and tremendous amount of customer contact interaction. And then if I have anything to add, I'll be happy to do so.

Marco Racanelli: Thank you, Russell. So it's hard always to pinpoint market share, particularly in the market that is growing as quickly and rapidly as this is growing, both on the silicon photonic and the silicon germanium side. And with a market that's growing at this rapid pace, there's obviously room for more than one player, and that's what we're seeing, as you described, a little bit of competition. What I can say is that we have -- we were the first to ramp in 200-millimeter to very high, not only capacity, but also very high yields with very good performance.

And as we just talked about previously, we were also the first to ramp in 300-millimeter with very high yields and very high quality and performance. So that is giving us confidence and giving our customers the confidence to extend the LTAs as we talked about, into 2029. So we're building capacity as quickly as we can, and all of that capacity is being spoken for almost immediately as we announce it, certainly well before it's even put in place with contracts from customers. So that's a tremendous position to be in. We also continue to invest at the leading edge of technology with our customers, having many Tier 1 customers with us.

We have incredible visibility over their needs of the future. And so putting in place technology that will pay dividends well into the future and not just today. So we anticipate not only short term maintaining very good market share, but certainly, there will be others competing with us in the market. And with growth as it is, that's perfectly understandable and okay.

But also in addition to the short term, are putting technology, 3.2T was talked about with both silicon indium phosphide, lithium niobate technologies and CPO, as we've talked about, both on the silicon photonics side and also silicon germanium side, putting technologies in place that will enable at least at the leading edge for us to maintain our competitive advantage and market share for the long term.

Russell Ellwanger: Thank you, Marco. I could just add, and I think this is a very important point to add. We really are engaged in billions of dollars of long-term agreements. Customers will never sign up to being the end of '26 now, not '27, not just '28, but 2029, unless they have faith that, number one, you can ship wafers on time at the highest quality. But secondly, that you will maintain a differentiated, more than competitive road map. What we are shipping now to lead customers for the most part, will not be a very big portion of what we're going to be shipping in 2029.

So the confidence that the customers have off of our relationship off of the programs that we're working on that are not just present, next, but generation plus 2 and in some cases, generation plus 3 type programs, that's what gives us the assurance. There will be competition. I mean it's a big market. It's a good market. It's a big enough market to afford competition. But we're quite confident in maintaining our leadership position because we are leaders, working with the leaders on leadership programs. And I think that, that's the biggest thing that I can say. What our market share will be, I mean, presently, I think it's extremely high. And one could check that with revenue.

I mean, look at just the Q3, close to $1 billion run rate on SiPho revenue. I think there's -- you'd be hard-pressed to find others that can come close to that. But Q4 breaking $1.1 billion, it's a pretty substantial place where we sit. But the biggest thing isn't the market share that we have now, it's the confidence in customers to sign up on long-term agreements through 2029 because those are committed. They're committed capacities. And they have to know us. We have to know them. There has to be a partnership and trust in order to go into those contracts.

And that's what really, for us, gives us confidence of maintaining a very high market share is that we are working truly with the best of the best on very advanced programs that -- it's a joke I have, but it's really true. I mean, for Kevin Costner in the Field of Dreams, if you build it, they will come as may be true. For us, we need very strong customer partners. And if we have the best of the best in each market, and we're working with them together on next-generation and generation plus 2 technologies, when we build it, it will be sold because we are dealing with the leaders. And so again, enough being said possibly.

But to give a specific market share number, I know what I think it is right now to say what it will be at the end of '27, '28, '29, that would really be proctology. But to say that we will maintain a very high differentiated market share on high technological differentiated products, I think that, that's very confident to be able to state.

Unknown Analyst: And I guess my follow-up was on another end market, the RF mobile. I think RF mobile is approaching the trough. It's in the low 50s this quarter. How should we think about the trajectory of RF mobile going into 2027, given on the last call, you mentioned the tape-out activities.

Russell Ellwanger: Mentioned what I'm sorry, please?

Unknown Analyst: Sorry, in terms of activities, how should we think about the trajectory of RF mobile?

Russell Ellwanger: For us, the trajectory is very strong. We had a bit of a dip in moving from Fab 7 to Fab 10, needing to requal multiple customers because of repurposing the Fab 7 really to focus on optical between the SiPho and the SiGe. It's going very well. We expect Q2, while Q1 was the highest shipments we've had, Q1 will be -- Q3 was Q4, Q1, Q2 should continue to grow, where Q2 will be absolute records. So I think it's -- for us, it's going extremely well. Again, I don't have a specific feel of the exact market share percentage. We are working with leaders and growing market share with the leaders.

And so I believe we're in very good shape. I also am quite confident that one of our programs isn't just a step function in capability. It's an absolutely opening of a new market capability itself. And that has not been formally released. We're working with at least one very lead customer on that type of figure of merit, and it's really a breakthrough figure of merit. Marco, is there anything else you would like to add there?

Marco Racanelli: No, I think you said it. We don't have the market share that we do in SiPho and RFSOI. There are multiple players, but we continue to lead at the very leading edge. So the market share that we have tends to be the very leading edge, the cream of the crop kind of piece of it, and that's what we're focusing on. We have limited capacity for RFSOI. Now we've dedicated Fab 10, and we use it for those leading components and leading technologies.

Operator: And we're going to take our final question for today and the question comes from the line of Richard Shannon from Craig-Hallum Capital Group.

Richard Shannon: Congratulations on great results again. Russell, let me follow up on a couple of comments you made on the call regarding SiPho, specifically on the laser attached side where it's not encompassed into the revenue model you've been talking about. Maybe you can talk about it in terms of a couple of different directions, one of which is how much content add do you have with laser integration or laser attach here? And over time, what percentage of your PICs would you expect to have laser attach and whatever -- I think there's multiple ways you can do it. What kind of attach rate do you see over time?

Russell Ellwanger: It's really multiple directions in the market. For integrated laser, it enters into a new served market that can be very big. There's multiple analysts that say that integrated laser will be a huge portion. There's others that really don't address it. I truly do not have a clear answer to it. Our lead customers there are very, very committed for growth with very strong forecast. And again, those are numbers that are not yet within the model, but they can be very appreciable, especially as one could imagine, there are appreciably higher ASPs. Against a very good baseline to begin with. So it's a good market to get in.

The die attach, though, is for more than just the indium phosphide laser. It's for an indium phosphide 400G modulator that we've already plus/minus demonstrated and for lithium niobate modulators. So the die attach that we're doing encompasses many different things, and it could be a very big portion of a 6.4T form factor of NPO or a pluggable with a 400 gigabit modulator.

Richard Shannon: Okay. I appreciate that perspective. My follow-on question is on the topic of NPO. You talked about greater than 10 customers on this call here. Maybe you can characterize kind of the customer set here across pluggable transceiver suppliers, historic ones, OEMs and even hyperscalers. And then how would you characterize kind of the competitive dynamics here? And ultimately, any qualitative commentary on market share that you expect in that product category over the next couple of years or so would be great to hear.

Russell Ellwanger: The existing customers that we have for pluggables all of our NPO customers are a subset of that. So we're not doing NPO with anybody that we haven't done pluggables with. It's an extension or a newer capability for a broader market. So it's not a different customer set whatsoever. One of the reasons I believe that we have so much engagement is as stated, it's the confidence and trust that's been built up through the engagement with pluggables. So that was the first part of your question. We expect to see an appreciable amount of NPO shipped in the second half of this coming year. That's our expectations and targets. Will it happen? It really depends on market adoption.

But it's the same set of customers that are just doing more, if you will, advanced programs with us, as stated earlier, Gen plus 1, Gen plus 2, Gen plus 3 programs are readily available between us and our premier customers. Marco, any color you'd like to add there?

Marco Racanelli: Yes. No, I think as you say, it will depend a little bit how big NPO gets for us in the short term will depend on the market adoption. The beauty for us is that we have strong share in both the pluggable and NPO. So if it's not NPO and it's pluggable, that's still Tower wafer being built. So -- and yes, I think as Russell indicated, it's most of our existing customers that are building NPO products with us. We haven't put that out in the public domain specifically with them, but we'll probably look to release some PRs so that it's in the public domain in the near future.

Operator: Dear speakers, there are no further questions for today. I would now like to hand the conference over to Russell Ellwanger for any closing remarks.

Russell Ellwanger: Thank you very much. Thank you for the questions. Just as a post summary comment, we had a corporate theme that we implemented, still have a corporate theme. It was implemented in 2025, and it was bold growth, limitless impact, infinite reach. We really adhere to that and try to breathe it in, in everything that we're doing. If you're bold in your growth, if you believe that you can have limitless impact, if you try to have infinite reach, you truly inspire the customers that you're working with as your partners. We had a very successful conference in Shenzhen, China, customer conference. We have in 1.5 weeks or so, our customer conference in Santa Clara, California, Technology Conference.

And it was a reunion of friends, and I can't overstate that. When you adhere and we really try to adhere to our values, we have what we call our value vectors, and it's leadership, partnership, impact and innovation. When we -- you adhere to those values and the definitions of them, I mean the true underlying definition of leadership, I think, is something that John F. Kennedy had stated, and that was leadership and learning are indispensable to each other. If you adhere to a partnership, which means truly working with your customers to adapt yourselves to what the market demands are and quickly, really doing it quickly. It drives unbelievable relationships as you have success together.

And that's what we see through our long-term agreements is a customer acknowledgment of the success that we've had together. We get a lot of joy in it. They get joy in it as success begets success, and it can never be overstated. Impact is very, very important. And impact really -- it deals with giving your people the power, capability and ownership to make change, to make things happen. A lot of our customers are amazed at the amount of young engineers that they interface with because we focus on the development of very high talented, high-potential people. And their growth is really dependent upon working with customers that inspire them.

There are 3 things that really enable success, and it's capability, environment and truly the motivation, your passion. If you have passion, you have capability and you create an environment of partnership where the customer feels open and that they can tell you whatever they want, you won't get offended, they can criticize where it has to get better, but also where we can tell them what they have to do better, what a relationship that becomes and what a truly blissful time it is an inspiring time. Where we talk about impact and innovation as well, and it's very, very critical, our model has been and continues to be very, very little drop from gross margin to operating margin.

I had stated it before, but at the $3.6 billion model that we put out, gross margin, 45% operating margin, 38%, a 7-point drop from gross to operating margin. And why is that critical for us? We want to stay lean on infrastructure because it allows us to be fast. And the faster we are, the more we delight our customers. If the questions -- well, not if, the questions about NPO, the questions about market share in the future, they're very, very critical. But how do we ensure that it happens, it's fast execution. And that is within our model of innovation because within innovation, sometimes the greatest innovation is simplification.

And simplification reduces the drop of gross margin to operating margin. So with that, I'd like to end the call. It's very, very exciting where we're at, where we're going. I really thank our investors for their interest in the company. I very much appreciate our customers for their faith and trust as demonstrated by the LTAs. And our employees worldwide are amazing. They give and give and get rewards, I think, that are commensurate with what they're doing, but their biggest reward is the joy of going home at the end of the day, believing that you've been successful, having the tools to have been successful.

We look forward to connecting with you at the upcoming conferences we'll be attending. Barclays 24th Annual Global Conference in San Francisco, December 10; Nomura at CES 27 in Las Vegas, 5th and 6th of January 27, the 29th Annual Needham Growth Conference in New York, the 12th and 13th of January. And as always, please analysts, investors, contact our Investor Relations department any time you have questions or wish to follow up. We very much enjoy your inputs. We get better through them. Thank you very much.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now all disconnect. Have a nice day.

news.Title: Tower Semiconductor Q3 Earnings Call Highlights
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Tower Semiconductor Ltd.? Here are five stocks we like better.

Record Q3 performance: Revenue rose 33% year over year to $526 million, while net profit increased to $120 million and diluted EPS reached $1.05. Management expects approximately $600 million in Q4 revenue, implying about $2 billion in 2026 revenue.

Silicon photonics is driving expansion: Q3 silicon photonics revenue reached roughly $240 million, with annualized capacity expected to exceed $1.1 billion in Q4. Tower is expanding production across four sites and expects 2027 capacity to support a run rate above $2.8 billion, backed by customer commitments extending through 2029.

Strong outlook and investment plan: Tower is developing near-packaged optics and advanced heterogeneous-integration products while investing $920 million in additional capacity. The company raised its long-term model to $3.6 billion in annual revenue, $1.38 billion in operating profit and a 33% net margin.

NVIDIA Just Named AI's Next Bottleneck—And These 3 Stocks Sit Right In It

Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM) reported record third-quarter results for 2026, citing accelerating demand for silicon photonics used in AI infrastructure and data-center connectivity, along with growth across its broader analog technology portfolio.

Revenue for the quarter reached $526 million, up 33% from $396 million in the third quarter of 2025 and 14% from $460 million in the prior quarter. Net profit rose to $120 million, or a 23% net margin, compared with $54 million and a 14% margin a year earlier. Diluted earnings per share were $1.05, compared with $0.47 in the prior-year period.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

Tower Semiconductor's AI Rally Is Built on a Light-Speed Bet

Chief Executive Officer Russell Ellwanger said the company expects fourth-quarter revenue at the midpoint of its guidance to reach $600 million. That result would bring full-year 2026 revenue to about $2 billion, compared with $1.57 billion in 2025.

Silicon Photonics Drives Growth Plans

Tower said silicon photonics revenue totaled approximately $240 million in the third quarter, representing an annualized rate near $1 billion. Ellwanger said the company expects its fourth-quarter silicon photonics annualized run rate to exceed $1.1 billion.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

Aeluma's Market Is Laser-Focused on Fresh Highs—Here's Why

The company is expanding silicon photonics production across four manufacturing sites to meet demand from customers serving AI-related optical interconnect markets. Tower expects year-end capacity to be about double the level that supported third-quarter silicon photonics revenue, with the additional capacity intended to support a revenue ramp during the first and second quarters of 2027.

Story Continues

Tower is also advancing its Track-1 300-millimeter expansion in Japan. Ellwanger said all tools for the expansion have been ordered and scheduled, with full production starts targeted for the third quarter of 2027. Including that expansion, the company expects silicon photonics start capacity to reach three times the level supporting third-quarter shipments.

→ LyondellBasell's Dividend Looks Safer, But a New Risk Could Change That

Management said that capacity is substantially covered through signed agreements and contracts in advanced negotiation stages. Customer commitments now extend into 2029, when Tower expects its Track-2 expansion in Japan to be underway. The company said its planned expansions will continue to be self-funded.

In response to an analyst question, Ellwanger said capacity expected by the third quarter of 2027 could support a silicon photonics run rate "somewhere a bit above a $2.8 billion" on a start-rate basis. He noted that figure does not include potential revenue from integrated laser products and other initiatives.

New Product Opportunities

Tower highlighted growing customer activity around near-packaged optics, or NPO, a technology that can more tightly integrate optical and electrical functions than conventional pluggable transceivers. The company said it is prototyping NPO products with more than 10 top customers and expects NPO products to carry a higher initial average selling price than pluggable products.

Ellwanger said the company expects an "appreciable amount" of NPO shipments in the second half of 2027, though the timing will depend on market adoption. Tower's NPO customers are currently a subset of its existing pluggable-transceiver customer base, he said.

The company also discussed heterogeneous integration efforts, including initial production for NewPhotonics using indium phosphide laser chiplets attached to silicon photonics wafers. Tower said it is deploying similar die-to-wafer attachment techniques with materials including thin-film lithium niobate for next-generation 400-gigabit-per-lane products.

President Marco Racanelli said Tower expects competition in the expanding silicon photonics and silicon germanium markets, but cited the company's production yields, customer relationships and technology roadmap as factors supporting its position. He said customers have extended long-term agreements through 2029, providing visibility into future capacity requirements.

Other Businesses and Utilization

Beyond optical technologies, Tower reported its highest quarterly RF-SOI revenue to date from its 300-millimeter Agrate, Italy, production corridor. The company also recorded a new high in product tape-outs for Fab 10, which serves its RF-SOI business.

Demand for Tower's BCD technologies grew about 10% year over year, according to Ellwanger, supported by AI and cloud data-center applications as well as mobile and automotive markets. Several strategic customers have entered long-term agreements at higher average selling prices, with Tower forecasting blended BCD pricing in 2027 to be 20% above 2026 levels.

In image sensors and displays, Tower began production of a high-speed global shutter sensor for high-end video cameras and said it is preparing capacity for expected customer demand in OLED-on-silicon displays during 2027.

All of Tower's 200-millimeter fabs operated at utilization rates of 85% to 90% during the third quarter, while its 300-millimeter fab remained fully utilized and above the company's 85% utilization model.

Margins, Capital Spending and Long-Term Model

Chief Financial Officer Oren Shirazi said gross profit increased 92% year over year to a record $179 million, while operating profit rose 2.5 times from the prior-year period to $127 million.

Tower is executing a previously announced $920 million capital investment program for silicon photonics and silicon germanium capacity and capabilities across facilities in Israel, Newport Beach, Texas and Japan. About 65% of the investment had been paid through the third quarter, with the remaining 35% expected to be paid in the fourth quarter of 2026 and the first half of 2027.

Shirazi said Tower expects a full return on investment from the $920 million program within one year. He added that quarterly incremental gross margin of roughly 62% was elevated because not all new equipment had begun depreciation, and reiterated a longer-term expectation for incremental gross profit margins of 55% to 58%.

The company updated its long-term financial model to target annual revenue of $3.6 billion, gross profit of $1.63 billion and operating profit of $1.38 billion. The model calls for annual net profit of $1.2 billion, representing a 33% net margin, based on assumptions including 85% fab utilization after planned capacity installations and qualifications are completed.

About Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ:TSEM)

Tower Semiconductor Ltd. is an Israeli specialty semiconductor foundry that manufactures integrated circuits for fabless semiconductor companies, integrated device manufacturers and system companies. The company provides process technologies and production services rather than selling branded end-user electronics.

Its offerings include analog and mixed-signal technologies, radio-frequency and high-voltage circuits, power management solutions, image sensors, and specialty memory products.

news.Title: Is UCTT Worth Buying as Growth Accelerates but Cash Flow Weakens?
news.Content:
Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. UCTT is benefiting from accelerating semiconductor equipment demand, with earnings and profitability moving sharply higher. The investment question is whether that operating momentum can overcome weak cash conversion and a capital-intensive expansion cycle.

That trade-off is especially important because stronger reported profits have not yet translated into equally strong cash generation or capital returns. Investors must weigh improving estimates and margins against funding needs, customer concentration and execution risk.

UCTT's Earnings Momentum Is Building

Third-quarter 2026 adjusted earnings reached $1.15 per share, topping the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 91 cents by 26.4%. Revenues increased 48.8% year over year to $759 million and exceeded the consensus estimate by 4.6%.

The outlook points to another step up if current expectations hold. The Zacks Consensus Estimate calls for fiscal 2027 revenues of $3.788 billion and earnings of $6.63 per share, compared with projected 2026 revenues of $2.768 billion and earnings of $3.40 per share.

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Ultra Clean Holdings, Inc. Quote

Ultra Clean Has a Clear Margin Opportunity

Profitability is improving as higher volumes increase factory utilization. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 17.3% in the third quarter, up from 16.7% sequentially, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 9% from 7%.

Management continues to target roughly 20% gross margin at about $4 billion of annual revenues. Higher utilization, greater vertical integration, a richer mix of engineered products and more production in lower-cost regions are expected to support that goal as capacity fills.

UCTT's Cash Conversion Is the Main Warning

The earnings improvement has not yet produced healthy cash conversion. Trailing 12-month cash-flow conversion was negative 244.4%, while free-cash-flow conversion was negative 418.5%, well below UCTT's historical medians.

Working capital is absorbing substantial cash. Inventory rose to $723.3 million, and operating activities used $42.3 million in the third quarter as Ultra Clean built critical components and safety stock. Trailing 12-month return on invested capital of 4.6% also remained below its 10-year company median of 9.8%.

Ultra Clean Still Carries Concentration Risk

Customer concentration remains a structural risk. Lam Research Corporation LRCX represented 39% of third-quarter revenues, while Applied Materials, Inc. AMAT accounted for 22%. Together, the two customers contributed 61%, leaving UCTT sensitive to their production schedules, sourcing decisions and wafer-fab-equipment spending.

Both customers are operating in supportive end markets. Lam reported September-quarter revenues of $8.22 billion and said AI was driving higher semiconductor demand and device complexity. Applied Materials posted record fiscal third-quarter revenues of $9.12 billion and cited AI-driven demand across leading-edge foundry-logic, DRAM and advanced packaging. Their strength supports the industry backdrop, but it does not remove UCTT's dependence on a small customer base.

Story Continues

UCTT's Ratings Favor Momentum Over Growth Quality

The bottom line is that UCTT offers accelerating earnings and a credible margin-expansion path, but the investment case is not clean. Cash conversion, low capital returns and concentration risk argue for discipline even as semiconductor demand strengthens.

UCTT currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which is favorable from an earnings-estimate revision perspective. Its Momentum Score of A adds support for near-term price and earnings momentum. However, the Growth Score of D, Value Score of C and VGM Score of C indicate a less consistent profile across growth quality, valuation and combined style characteristics. That mix favors investors who prioritize momentum while recognizing that cash-flow and execution issues remain unresolved. news.Title: 3 Tech Stocks Boosting Buyback Capacity in the Face of the Sector's Recent Tumble
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in Amphenol Corporation? Here are five stocks we like better.

Amid a tech sector sell-off, NXP Semiconductors, Amphenol and F5 announced large buyback authorizations signaling confidence in their future prospects.

NXP added $5 billion in buyback capacity as data center demand grows, while Amphenol unveiled a $4 billion repurchase program alongside a 20% dividend increase.

F5 announced an additional $1.5 billion buyback despite a 20.4% post-earnings stock drop, and analysts see over 40% upside for Amphenol shares.

Investors have hit tech stocks hard over the past few weeks. The Technology Select Sector SPDR Fund (NYSEARCA: XLK), a commonly used proxy for the sector's performance, is down more than 7% in October. Fears around the AI buildout's sustainability and disappointing earnings reports from Big Tech have been key drivers of the decline.

Amid the sell-off, three notable tech stocks are signaling confidence in the future by announcing substantial buyback authorizations. This list includes one name that has ridden the AI wave higher and higher, and others that are just now starting to participate more meaningfully.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

NXP's Data Center Demand Picks Up, Adds Huge Buyback Capacity

First up is NXP Semiconductors (NASDAQ: NXPI), a chip stock that is up approximately 17% in 2026. NXP's business primarily serves automotive and industrial customers. While NXP has not been a huge AI winner thus far, data center demand is starting to pick up, with the company expecting its data center revenue to exceed $500 million in 2026. NXP believes this business will scale to over $1 billion in the coming years, and sees physical AI as a long-term growth opportunity.

During its latest earnings call, the firm made a significant buyback announcement, adding an incremental $5 billion in repurchase capacity. This brings the company's total buyback capacity to $6.3 billion. With a market capitalization near $66 billion, this represents around 9.5% of the firm's value, giving it substantial buyback firepower.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

The company also notes that the authorization positions it to accelerate buybacks beginning in Q4, suggesting that its repurchases will increase compared to recent quarters. In Q3, the company spent $103 million on buybacks, significantly below its long-term average.

The planned acceleration suggests the company may see its shares as a strong value at recent levels.

Story Continues

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

AI Winner Amphenol Announces $4 Billion Buyback Program

In contrast to NXP, Amphenol (NYSE: APH) has been a massive beneficiary of the AI boom so far. The stock has posted a moderate but still strong return near 18% in 2026. This comes after shares soared 41% in 2024 and another 96% in 2025.

The connector, cable and sensor maker saw its revenue rise 65% year-over-year (YOY) last quarter to a record $10.2 billion. The company's acquisition of CommScope significantly increased its growth rate, but sales still grew by 37% YOY on an organic basis. Meanwhile, orders increased 99% YOY, with a book-to-bill ratio of 1.19:1, signaling continued demand momentum.

Amphenol indicated confidence in its long-term outlook by announcing a three-year, $4 billion repurchase program. This plan will become effective at the beginning of 2027, with the firm expecting to exhaust the capacity under its previous program by the end of 2026.

Given Amphenol's size, the program represents only about 2.1% of its market capitalization. However, the company is also returning more capital to shareholders through higher dividends. Amphenol announced a 20% dividend increase, after accounting for its recent stock split, moving its payout to 15 cents per share. Amphenol's forward yield is approximately 0.77%.

F5 Holds Huge Buyback Capacity After Dramatic Sell-Off

Last up is cybersecurity company F5 (NASDAQ: FFIV). Despite the market clobbering shares after its latest earnings report, F5 has performed strongly in 2026, up around 32%. Prior to its 20.4% post-earnings drop, F5 shares were up around 80% on the year.

This decline came even as F5 handily beat estimates on sales and earnings per share (EPS). Revenue increased by 13% YOY to $917 million, around $33 million higher than expected. Meanwhile, EPS of $4.42 was 16 cents higher than expected. The company also saw its AI-related offerings exceed $100 million in bookings, up 300% YOY. The bookings primarily came from AI data delivery offerings.

F5 pointed to a slowdown in its forecast for fiscal year 2027, projecting revenue growth of 8% to 9%, down from 11% in 2026.

The company also cited margin pressure as it grapples with higher component costs and invests in pursuing AI opportunities. These factors influenced the stock's sell-off.

During its earnings call, F5 announced an additional $1.5 billion share repurchase program, bringing its total capacity to $1.8 billion. One silver lining of F5's stock price decline is that this added capacity can now buy back many more shares than it otherwise could. F5's buyback capacity is now equal to around 9% of its market capitalization, a hefty figure.

Analysts Eye 40% Upside in Amphenol

Analysts see substantial upside ahead for Amphenol, even after the stock's impressive gains over the past few years. The MarketBeat consensus price target near $112 implies more than 40% upside.

IT datacom sales represented 48% of the company's revenue last quarter, and three-fourths of those sales were related to AI. IT datacom also drove massive growth, increasing 117% YOY in the United States. In turn, Amphenol's fortunes largely depend on the continued expansion of AI data centers, making hyperscaler capital expenditure guidance for 2027 critical to watch.

news.Title: Deciphering KLA (KLAC) International Revenue Trends
news.Content:
Have you looked into how KLA (KLAC) performed internationally during the quarter ending September 2026? Considering the widespread global presence of this maker of equipment for manufacturing semiconductors, examining the trends in international revenues is essential for assessing its financial resilience and prospects for growth.

In the modern, closely-knit global economic landscape, the capacity of a business to access foreign markets is often a key determinant of its financial well-being and growth path. Investors now place great importance on grasping the extent of a company's dependence on international markets, as it sheds light on the firm's earnings stability, its skill in leveraging various economic cycles and its broad growth potential.

International market involvement serves as insurance against economic downturns at home and enables engagement with economies that are growing more quickly. Still, this move toward diversification is not without its challenges, as it involves navigating through the fluctuations of currencies, geopolitical threats, and the distinctive nature of various markets.

While analyzing KLAC's performance for the last quarter, we found some intriguing trends in revenues from its overseas segments that Wall Street analysts commonly model and monitor.

The company's total revenue for the quarter amounted to $4.14 billion, showing rise of 28.9%. We will now explore the breakdown of KLAC's overseas revenue to assess the impact of its international operations.

Unveiling Trends in KLAC's International Revenues

During the quarter, Europe & Israel contributed $194.33 million in revenue, making up 4.7% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $180.94 million, this meant a surprise of +7.4%. Looking back, Europe & Israel contributed $355.64 million, or 9.7%, in the previous quarter, and $150.98 million, or 4.7%, in the same quarter of the previous year.

Of the total revenue, $497.17 million came from Korea during the last fiscal quarter, accounting for 12%. This represented a surprise of -27.28% as analysts had expected the region to contribute $683.66 million to the total revenue. In comparison, the region contributed $374.09 million, or 10.2%, and $299.37 million, or 9.3%, to total revenue in the previous and year-ago quarters, respectively.

Taiwan generated $1.02 billion in revenues for the company in the last quarter, constituting 24.7% of the total. This represented a surprise of -10.69% compared to the $1.15 billion projected by Wall Street analysts. Comparatively, in the previous quarter, Taiwan accounted for $1.14 billion (31.1%), and in the year-ago quarter, it contributed $793.61 million (24.7%) to the total revenue.

Story Continues

Japan accounted for 3.9% of the company's total revenue during the quarter, translating to $159.78 million. Revenues from this region represented a surprise of -53.19%, with Wall Street analysts collectively expecting $341.37 million. When compared to the preceding quarter and the same quarter in the previous year, Japan contributed $210.48 million (5.8%) and $295.21 million (9.2%) to the total revenue, respectively.

China accounted for 34.5% of the company's total revenue during the quarter, translating to $1.43 billion. Revenues from this region represented a surprise of +41.88%, with Wall Street analysts collectively expecting $1 billion. When compared to the preceding quarter and the same quarter in the previous year, China contributed $956.73 million (26.2%) and $1.27 billion (39.5%) to the total revenue, respectively.

During the quarter, Rest of Asia contributed $218.23 million in revenue, making up 5.3% of the total revenue. When compared to the consensus estimate of $140.74 million, this meant a surprise of +55.06%. Looking back, Rest of Asia contributed $158.04 million, or 4.3%, in the previous quarter, and $105.47 million, or 3.3%, in the same quarter of the previous year.

Revenue Projections for Overseas Markets

The current fiscal quarter's total revenue for KLA, as projected by Wall Street analysts, is expected to reach $4.71 billion, reflecting an increase of 43% from the same quarter last year. The breakdown of this revenue by foreign region is as follows: Europe & Israel is anticipated to contribute 4.4% or $207.61 million, Korea 15.7% or $737.99 millionTaiwan 28.5% or $1.34 billionJapan 8.9% or $417.55 millionChina 24.5% or $1.16 billion and Rest of Asia 3.4% or $161.39 million.

For the full year, the company is projected to achieve a total revenue of $18.3 billion, which signifies a rise of 34.7% from the last year. The share of this revenue from various regions is expected to be: Europe & Israel at 4.7% ($865.98 million), Korea at 16.1% ($2.95 billion), Taiwan at 29.4% ($5.38 billion), Japan at 8.6% ($1.58 billion), China at 26.4% ($4.83 billion), and Rest of Asia at 3.8% ($698.85 million).

The Bottom Line

KLA's leaning on foreign markets for its revenue stream presents a mix of chances and challenges. Therefore, a vigilant watch on its international revenue movements can greatly aid in projecting the company's future direction.

In a world where international interdependencies and geopolitical conflicts are ever-increasing, Wall Street analysts closely monitor these trends for companies having international presence to adjust their earnings forecasts. Of course, there are several other factors, including a company's standing within its home borders, that influence analysts' earnings forecasts.

We at Zacks strongly focus on the dynamic earnings forecast of companies, given that empirical studies have demonstrated its potent impact on the immediate price movement of stocks. Invariably, there's a positive relationship -- upward earnings predictions often result in an increase in stock prices.

Boasting a remarkable track record that's been externally verified, the Zacks Rank, our unique stock rating system, leverages changes in earnings projections to function as a reliable gauge for predicting short-term stock price movements.

Currently, KLA holds a Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy), signifying its potential to outperform the overall market's performance in the forthcoming period. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Assessing KLA's Stock Price Movement in Recent Times
