news.Title: STMicroelectronics Could Reach New Highs—Here's What Needs to Happen
news.Content:
Key Points

Interested in STMicroelectronics N.V.? Here are five stocks we like better.

STMicroelectronics stock, despite a near 50% correction in 2026, is technically positioned for a third Elliott Wave move toward fresh all-time highs.

The company posted Q3 revenue of $3.76 billion, up 17.9%, with widening margins, surging free cash flow, and bullish guidance pointing to mid-20% growth in Q4.

Analysts maintain a consensus Moderate Buy rating with 50% upside potential.

STMicroelectronics (NYSE: STM) stock price action is set up for a big move that could take it to all-time highs. While STM suffered an ugly price correction of nearly 50%, which suggested a market implosion, investors shouldn't get it wrong.

The correction that took place in Q2 and Q3 2026 was a mechanism within a rapidly swelling market.

→ L3Harris Stock Took a Beating—Is a 20% Rebound Next?

STM's fundamental story is a legacy business becoming a next-gen AI enabler, with rapidly expanding margins and ample free cash flow, cementing its already central position in the tech landscape.

The stock price story follows suit: a legacy market transitioning to one in which free cash flow is growing at a high triple-digit pace, expected to remain strong in the coming year and underpin capital returns.

→ Starbucks Says Its Turnaround Is Done—The Numbers Make a Strong Case (With 1 Catch)

The shift is reflected in trading volume, which took a decidedly bullish turn in 2024 and has trended higher ever since.

Technically, STM is in the midst of an Elliott Wave cycle that has yet to play out.

→ Marvell Eyes a Swing for the AI Networking Fences as Markets Weigh Lumentum Price Tag

The initial and second upwaves are complete, and the market is set up for a third move that could take STM's price to fresh highs.

Strong Q3 Results and Bullish Guidance Set the Stage for 2027

STMicroelectronics posted a solid Q3, with revenue up 17.9% to $3.76 billion, narrowly beating consensus. Growth was broad across channels, led by a 46% increase in the RF Optical segment, critical for data centers and high-speed data transmission. By end market, sales to original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) grew 10.2%, while sales to distribution centers rose nearly 39%, and total sales are expected to remain strong in the coming quarters as demand outpaces supply.

Margin news was mixed, but with a silver lining. The company missed consensus for adjusted earnings because higher capital expenditure (CapEx) obscured strengths revealed by internal metrics. Gross and operating margins widened by more than 400 basis points, driving triple-digit increases in cash and free cash flow. Operating cash flow more than doubled to $1.02 billion, leaving free cash flow (FCF) at $351 million, despite higher CapEx, up 2.7x from the prior year and a 9.3% FCF margin.

Story Continues

Guidance is a catalyst for this market, likely to be compounded by similarly strong results and forecasts in the upcoming quarters. STM provided a hot guide for Q4, expecting revenue above consensus, up more than 10% sequentially and accelerating into the mid-20% range versus last year. Factors suggesting the guide is cautious and that strengths will continue include the book-to-bill ratio, which came in well above 3. At this pace, the backlog is growing at three times the pace of revenue, setting the stage for a robust 2027.

Analysts and Institutions See 50% Upside for STMicroelectronics

Analysts expressed some caution in their initial responses to the earnings release, highlighting high expectations and the potential for investors to be dissatisfied with the gross margin, as good as it was.

That said, the net response reaffirmed the consensus Moderate Buy rating and the forecast for 50% upside, with analysts focused on the growth trajectory, cash flow, and expansion plans.

CapEx increases fund a multi-year AI-focused expansion plan. It aims to optimize existing capacity and focus on optical connectivity, the key to unlocking AI's power.

Institutions and other sell-side interests reflect confidence in this stock and its value. Institutions own about 75% of the stock across U.S. and home-listed shares and are accumulating it at discounted prices.

Short-sellers, the other sell-side interest, are largely absent, providing no headwind for share prices. The likely outcome is that institutions continue to support the market at or near $45, if not slowly lift support over time, providing a base for the next big rally.

STMicroelectronics Has Major Catalysts Ahead

STMicroelectronics has three big catalysts that can trigger its rebound and sustain the upward trajectory: margin recovery, an EV inflection, and monetizing its investments in optical connects.

Margin recovery is expected to continue in Q4, potentially to pre-expansion levels. If so, it signals successful optimization and may prompt aggressive re-rating from analysts.

The EV inflection is an industry-wide phenomenon underpinned by inventory normalization and may generate a definitive data point in STM's upcoming report, another catalyst for analysts.

Monetization of AI investments is the final piece, cementing the company's transition to a next-gen AI enabler.

Risks include execution, with manufacturing footprint changes key to expansion, customer concentration, and end-market cyclicality. Clients are centered in big-name hyperscalers and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), which accounts for a low-double-digit percentage of revenue, while market cyclicality may soon end. The automotive market is the root of cyclical weaknesses, which may be mitigated by the rise of physical AI and the Internet of Things (IoT), which will rely on many of the same microcontrol products.

news.Title: A big sell-off collides with more Big Tech earnings and a midterm election: What to watch this week
news.Content:
Last week, we opened the Morning Brief newsletter by saying the first week of Big Tech earnings looked promising — until Thursday. This time, we're here to say the second week of Big Tech earnings looked promising — until Tuesday.

Lackluster earnings from Alphabet ( GOOG ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Intel ( INTC ) sent the tech complex into a steep sell-off, ending a wild week that began with Anthropic's S-1 filing.

Coming into this week, all eyes will be on potential sparks to relight the fire under the tech sector. Fire, to be clear, in a bad way.

Kicking off the week on Monday are earnings from Apple ( AAPL ) and Palantir ( PLTR ), alongside Tower Semiconductor ( TSEM ) and Lattice Semiconductor ( LSCC ) in the chips sector.

On Tuesday, our focus shifts to politics, as US midterms are set to influence everything from control of Congress and the Iran war to the data center boom. On top of that, AMD ( AMD ) and Marathon Petroleum Corporation ( MPC ) both report earnings, and the US government will report JOLTS data in the first major labor market update of the week.

Wednesday and Thursday bring earnings from Toyota Motor ( TM ), ConocoPhillips ( COP ), Eaton Corporation ( ETN ), Arm Holdings ( ARM ), McDonald's ( MCD ), and a range of other corporate market heavyweights, alongside a smattering of economic data.

And all of that excitement sets up Friday's October nonfarm payrolls report, the banner data release of the week.

Big Tech's sell-off wasn't about the actual fundamentals

It was a deeply red week for the tech sector after a slew of earnings failed to give investors the signs of strength they were looking (and hoping) for.

At Alphabet, a miss on both revenue and profit sent shares falling 13% as Sundar Pichai said that while the company's search division had grown, the money wasn't keeping up as AI cuts into search monetization.

Down the street at Amazon, a double miss on both earnings and revenue triggered a sell-off that couldn't be stopped by strong cloud growth in AWS.

And we can't forget Intel, where a beat on earnings and in-line revenue were overshadowed by weakness in PC sales, attributed to heightened memory costs. That company lost a quarter of its value after the report, falling over 28%.

But there's a conundrum for investors in these earnings reports. As Barron's associate editor Al Root said to Yahoo Finance, the numbers weren't all bad; it's more like investors have gotten more demanding.

"It's not that the earnings were awful, it's just that it wasn't enough to support the market," Root said on "The 8:30." He added, "The level of nerves going into earnings season was so high, like everybody was waiting for the shoe to drop."

Story Continues

At Amazon, the company's AWS unit — effectively, its data center and AI beating heart — reported revenue of $45.9 billion, representing growth of 40% and healthily exceeding estimates. Alphabet's cloud unit brought in $30.7 billion where analysts had only seen $29.1 billion.

Intel's data center and AI segment pulled down $7.318 billion against estimates of $6.675 billion expected, marking 78% growth year on year, while Sandisk ( SNDK ) beat on both the top and bottom lines yet still got pulled into a sell-off.

To quote Evercore ISI's Mark Mahaney, writing about Amazon, "This was an expectations correction and not a fundamentals correction."

The crypto fallout from the Binance heist

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, was hit late Thursday by what investigators say is the biggest crypto hack in history. with $6.3 billion in digital assets affected. It might just be the biggest heist of all time.

In the immediate aftermath, Binance said it has temporarily suspended customer withdrawals. Binance added it "will cover all losses" using its Secure Asset Fund for users and company reserves. "User funds are safe," the exchange said, adding that it temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed.

But that didn't stop other major crypto assets from tumbling, led by ether ( ETH-USD ), which dropped 4% to around $2,200. Binance's native token, BNB ( BND-USD ), also plunged by more than 5%.

The question for the crypto industry writ large will be: What comes next, after a multibillion-dollar heist off the largest cryptocurrency exchange on the market?

"The industry has to wake up to the point that they have to protect the customer funds," Owen Lau, managing director at Clear Street, told Yahoo Finance on "The 8:30," adding, "They have to have a pretty good cybersecurity system to give more confidence to people."

After the news initially broke, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong said on X that his platform had reached out to Binance to offer assistance, and that his team would do "everything we can to support in the current situation." He added that "moments like this call for the industry to work together." (Disclosure: Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.)

With the industry pursuing legislation in Washington that would meaningfully shift its regulatory landscape toward the banking world, how does it adapt after such an attack, and how does it earn trust?

"We need a good regulatory framework to really protect the industry and also give confidence to investors," Lau said. "Right now, we don't have it."

A wild week in Washington awaits with a pivotal midterm election

It's a busy week in Washington, to say the least.

Not only will there be 470 active elections — all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats — for the country to pore over, but Friday will bring the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly nonfarm payrolls report, a key check on the labor market.

There's an argument to be made that the jobs report is downstream of the midterms in multiple ways. Two of the banner issues in these races — the cost of living and the trajectory of AI — are set to play key roles in determining how the labor market shifts over the next few years.

A particularly big focus for investors is the key races set to make big determinations on the direction of states' data center development pipelines. Races to watch include the Ohio Senate election between Democratic candidate Sherrod Brown and Republican Jon Husted, and the Texas gubernatorial election between incumbent Republican Greg Abbott and Democrat Gina Hinojosa.

Keep a close eye on California, too, as voters take to the polls to determine the fate of Proposition 40, the proposed billionaire wealth tax that saw Meta issue new shares to protect CEO Mark Zuckerberg's voting power in case he has to sell shares to pay it.

All that said, strategists caution that companies make decisions on a longer-term basis than one single election cycle.

"The historic investment hyperscalers make in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure today is done so with the aim of growing earnings over the next decade and even longer," Seth Meyer, global head of client portfolio management at JanusHenderson Investors, wrote. "When allocating capital over such horizons, management teams factor in potential changes in the macroeconomic cycle and regulatory environment."

On the labor data front, economists are looking for Friday's nonfarm payrolls report to show 55,000 jobs added, coming after a report well below estimates that showed 29,000 jobs added last month. Zooming in, that entire +55,000 balance is expected to be made up in the private sector, and manufacturing is expected to see zero jobs added or lost even given the data center construction boom.

One of the key arguments for the Federal Reserve's ability to raise rates in September — and its potential to do so again in December — is strength in the labor market. Any perceived weakness could complicate that outlook.

news.Title: 櫃買指數逆勢翻紅漲近1%！分析師點名環球晶當「多頭司令」
news.Content:
台股今（2）日一度挫逾800點，但櫃買指數卻率先由黑翻紅，盤中上漲近1%，表現相對強勢。啟發投顧分析師丁彥鈞表示，櫃買指數主要是技術面跌深反彈，KD指標已降至20附近，但不代表長線跌勢結束，後續仍可能有約1成修正空間。若上櫃股展開反彈，他看好群聯（8299）、環球晶（6488），其中又以環球晶有望成為上櫃股反彈的「多頭司令」。

觀察今日盤勢，櫃買指數早盤最低下探362.18點，隨後買盤回流，由黑翻紅，盤中最高來到373.22點。相較加權指數，中小型股表現相對強勢。

丁彥鈞指出，櫃買指數近期已跌破半年線，技術面明顯轉弱，但隨著KD指標降至20附近，短線出現跌深反彈。他強調，今天盤中翻紅主要是技術性反彈。

丁彥鈞表示，櫃買指數目前本益比約25.77倍，仍處於相對偏高水準，若未來美國升息、外資持續賣超，本益比可能向20倍靠攏，但不代表指數還會再下跌2成，因為企業的獲利有成長，預估櫃買指數可能再下跌1成左右。

至於哪些上櫃股有機會率先帶動反彈，丁彥鈞點名群聯及環球晶，認為兩家公司基本面較佳，有望成為後續反彈的觀察指標。若只能選出一檔作為「多頭司令」，他則看好環球晶，主要是環球晶位於半導體產業上游，對景氣變化的反應較為敏感。

丁彥鈞也預估，櫃買指數350點附近有機會形成支撐，跌破的機率不高。不過，他提醒，短線跌深反彈與長線趨勢反轉仍有差別，投資人不宜僅因指數盤中翻紅，就認定修正行情已經結束。

湯暖萱／財經特派記者，主跑主計處、營建、百貨紡織等
